The receipt tracks its own billing state through **Status**: it is created as **To Bill**, and moves to **Billed** when a Purchase Invoice is raised against it — returning to **To Bill** if that invoice is cancelled. A separate **Posting Status** of `Pending`, `Started`, or `Posted` records how far the receipt's own stock and ledger postings have progressed.

As quantities are received, **Qty Purchased** on the originating Purchase Order lines is updated and the order's status is re-derived.

### Validations

- Each item is checked against the **budget** allocated to it or to its item group.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing receipt.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier** and **Supplier Inv No / Supplier Inv Date** - The party and their reference for the delivery.
- **Purchase Order** - The order the receipt is raised against.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are received into.
- **Items** - Received items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Status** - `To Bill` until a Purchase Invoice is raised, then `Billed`.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the receipt's stock and ledger postings.
- **Payment Schedule** - Planned settlement dates and amounts for the receipt.
- **Project / Default Cost Center** - Costing dimensions for the receipt.
- **Update Rates In Price List** - Writes the received rates back to the price list.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Purchase Return
entries.content:
The **Purchase Return** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods sent back to a supplier and reduces the amount payable accordingly.

### Purpose

To take returned goods out of stock and reverse their financial effect — reducing the supplier liability, the inventory value, and the input tax originally claimed.

### How It Works

A return is raised against a **Supplier** from a **Warehouse**, and its lines reference the original **Purchase Invoice** line being returned. The **Invoices** table records which invoices the return is set against.

On submission the return issues the goods out of the warehouse and posts the reversal to the general ledger:

- The **Accounts Payable account is debited** with the rounded total, reducing what is owed to the supplier.
- The **Inventory account is credited** with the value excluding tax.
- The **Tax account is credited** with the tax total, reversing the input tax.
- Any **round off** is posted to the round off account.

Where the return is not a credit purchase, payment postings are made as well, so a return against a cash purchase settles immediately rather than sitting on the payable.

If the return carries a **Payment Schedule**, the corresponding schedule entries are rebuilt against the return, replacing any that existed before.

### Validations

- The quantity returned cannot exceed what remains available on the original purchase line. The check is cumulative — all other returns already raised against that line are counted, so a line cannot be over-returned across several documents.
- Stock must exist in the warehouse and be sufficient for the quantity being returned, unless the Company has **Allow Negative Stock** enabled.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier** - Party the goods are returned to.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are issued from.
- **Items** - Returned items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and the reference to the original purchase line.
- **Invoices** - The purchase invoices the return is set against.
- **Credit Purchase** - Determines whether the return reduces the payable or settles immediately.
- **Payment Schedule** - Rebuilt against the return where settlement is scheduled.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the return's stock and ledger postings.
- **Project / Default Cost Center** - Costing dimensions for the return.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Buying Document Flow
entries.content:
The buying documents in **DIGITZ ERP** are connected by rules that decide which document may be raised from which, and what is still outstanding.

### Material Request to Purchase Order

An approved **Material Request** with the purpose `Purchase` can be turned into a **Purchase Order**. Only lines with an approved quantity that has not yet been fully ordered are carried over, and each order line keeps a reference back to the request line so the request's purchased quantity stays current.

### Purchase Order onward — two routes, not both

From a submitted Purchase Order the goods can be recorded either through a **Purchase Receipt** first, or straight onto a **Purchase Invoice**. The system enforces that only one route is taken for a given order:

- A **Purchase Receipt** cannot be created when a submitted Purchase Invoice already references the order without a receipt.
- A **Purchase Invoice** cannot be created when the order is already linked to a Purchase Receipt — the invoice must be raised from that receipt instead.
- The Purchase Order must be **submitted** before an invoice can be created from it.
- Creation stops if the order has **no pending items** left, and if any line has a conversion factor of zero or less.

Use the receipt route when goods arrive before the bill; use the direct invoice route when the bill accompanies the goods.

### Purchase Receipt to Purchase Invoice

A **Purchase Invoice** can be generated from a Purchase Receipt, carrying the supplier, warehouse, terms, dates, and lines across. On submission the receipt's status becomes **Billed**, and the value held in Stock Received But Not Billed is cleared into the supplier liability. Cancelling the invoice returns the receipt to **To Bill**.

### Purchase Return

A **Purchase Return** is raised against **Purchase Invoice** lines rather than against orders or receipts, since it is the billed quantity that determines what may be returned.

### What each stage affects

| Document | Stock | General Ledger |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Order | — | — |
| Purchase Receipt | Goods in | Inventory debited, Stock Received But Not Billed credited |
| Purchase Invoice | Goods in, when raised without a receipt | Supplier liability, expense, and tax |
| Purchase Return | Goods out | Payable debited; inventory and tax reversed |

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Buying Reports
entries.content:
The **Buying Reports** in **DIGITZ ERP** present the purchase documents as registers, as itemwise detail, and as period analysis.

### Registers

**Purchase Register**, **Purchase Order Register**, and **Purchase Return Register** list the documents of each type over a period with their supplier, dates, and values — the document-level view of what was ordered, purchased, and returned.

### Itemwise detail and summaries

Each register has an itemwise pair. The **Itemwise Register** reports break the documents down to their individual lines, and the **Itemwise Summary Report** consolidates those lines by item:

- **Purchase Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Purchase Order Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Order Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Purchase Return Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Return Itemwise Summary Report**

Use the register when a specific transaction must be traced, and the summary when the question is how much of an item was bought or returned in total.

### Analysis

**Periodic Purchase Analysis Report** and **Periodic Expense Analysis Report** present purchases and expenses across periods for comparison rather than for tracing individual documents.

**Purchase Payment Analysis Report** shows purchases against what has been paid, for reviewing the settlement position with suppliers.

**Projectwise Purchase Receipt Report** groups received goods by project, for projects where materials are purchased and consumed against a specific job.

**Buying Chart - Top Supplier Purchases** ranks suppliers by purchase value, giving a quick view of where spend is concentrated.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Module Overview
entries.content:
The **Selling Module** in **DIGITZ ERP** covers the sale of goods and services from the first quotation through to delivery, invoicing, and any goods returned.

The cycle runs **Quotation → Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice**, with **Sales Return** handling goods taken back from the customer. Each stage carries its quantities and rates forward, and each records how much of the preceding document has been consumed — so what remains outstanding on an order is always visible.

The stages divide by what they affect:

- **Quotation** is an offer. It creates neither stock nor accounting entries, and must be marked **Won** before it can be converted.
- **Sales Order** is a confirmed commitment. It also posts nothing; it tracks how much of what was ordered has since been delivered or invoiced.
- **Delivery Note** handles the **physical movement** — goods leave the warehouse and their cost is recognised.
- **Sales Invoice** handles the **financial posting** — customer receivable, income, and tax. It is documented under the Accounting module; see [Sales Invoice](#sales-invoice).
- **Sales Return** reverses both, bringing goods back into stock and reducing the receivable.

**Tab Sales** provides a shorter path for counter sales, producing a Sales Invoice directly.

Progress across the whole cycle can be followed on the **Sales Flow** dashboard, which brings every stage of a customer transaction onto one screen; see [Sales Flow](#sales-flow).

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Customer
entries.content:
The **Customer** in **DIGITZ ERP** is the party master for everything the company sells.

### Purpose

To hold one record per customer — identity, contacts, delivery locations, tax registration, credit arrangement, and default pricing — which every selling document draws from.

### How It Works

Customers are identified by **Customer Name**. Each carries a **Default Price List**, from which selling documents take their rates, and may carry **Default Terms**; where **Use Default Customer Terms** is set, the company-level terms apply instead.

The credit arrangement is held as **Credit Days** and a **Credit Amount** limit, and flows into the credit fields on selling documents. The customer's **Tax Id** is carried onto sales documents as the tax registration.

Customers are classified by **Customer Group** — a name and a disabled flag — and located by **Area**, which is itself grouped by **Emirate**. A **Salesman** can be assigned, linking the customer to an Employee for reporting. Multiple **Delivery Locations** can be recorded and selected as the ship-to location on individual documents.

Where a customer originated as a lead, the **Prospect** field links back to the **Sales Prospect** record it was converted from.

Two flags affect reporting and access: **Exclude From Showing In SOA** keeps the customer out of statement of account output, and **Disabled** retires a customer without removing history.

### Customer-specific pricing

Beyond the default price list, the **Item** master carries a **Customer Prices** table. When a Sales Order is submitted, the rate used for each line is written back as that customer's rate for that item, dated with the order's posting date — and an existing entry is only replaced when the new date is later. Whether these remembered rates are then applied to new documents is controlled by **Use Customer Last Price** in the Company settings.

### Key Fields

- **Customer Name** - Name and identifier of the customer.
- **Customer Group** - Classification the customer belongs to.
- **Default Price List** - Price list selling documents take rates from.
- **Credit Days / Credit Amount** - The credit arrangement agreed with the customer.
- **Tax Id** - Tax registration number, carried onto sales documents.
- **Delivery Locations** - Ship-to locations selectable on selling documents.
- **Salesman** - Employee responsible for the account.
- **Area, Emirate, Country, Address Line 1 and 2** - Location details, also assembled into a **Full Address**.
- **Contact Person, Designation, Phone, Mobile No, Email** - Contact details.
- **Default Currency** - Currency the customer is billed in.
- **Prospect** - The Sales Prospect this customer was converted from.
- **Exclude From Showing In SOA** - Omits the customer from statement of account output.
- **Disabled** - Retires the customer without removing history.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Quotation
entries.content:
The **Quotation** in **DIGITZ ERP** records a priced offer made to a customer or a prospect.

### Purpose

To state what is being offered, at what price, and on what terms — and to record the outcome of the offer so that won and lost business can be analysed.

### How It Works

A quotation is raised for a **Customer** or, through **Lead From = Prospect**, for a **Sales Prospect** that has not yet become a customer. Rates come from the selected **Price List**, and each line carries the item, quantity, unit, rate, tax, and any discount. The rounded total is also written out **in words**.

A quotation posts **nothing** — no stock movement and no ledger entry. It is an offer until its outcome is recorded.

The outcome is held in **Status**, which is `Pending`, `Won`, or `Lost`. A won quotation can record a **Won Reason** and a lost one a **Lost Reason**, both drawn from their own master lists so the reasons stay consistent and reportable.

**A quotation must be marked Won before a Sales Order can be created from it.** Attempting to convert a quotation in any other status is refused. The conversion option is only offered while the quotation has not already been used — once a Sales Order, Delivery Note, or Sales Invoice exists against it, it cannot be converted again. Where the quotation was raised for a prospect, the system first checks that a Customer exists for that prospect.

A quotation can be **duplicated** into a fresh quotation carrying the same customer, terms, totals, and lines — the practical way to issue a revision, alongside the **Rev.No** and **Rev Date** fields kept for print. Recurring sets of lines can be pulled in from a **Quotation Items Template** rather than entered by hand.

Where the company has **Manual Quotation No** enabled, the quotation is named by the number entered on the document rather than by the automatic series.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** or **Prospect** with **Lead From** - Who the offer is made to.
- **Status** - `Pending`, `Won`, or `Lost`; must be `Won` to convert.
- **Won Reason / Lost Reason** - The recorded outcome, from their master lists.
- **Price List** and **Rate Includes Tax** - How rates are sourced and whether they are tax-inclusive.
- **Items** - Offered items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Quotation Item Template** - A saved set of lines to populate the quotation from.
- **Salesman** - Employee the offer is credited to.
- **Ship To Location** - Delivery location selected from the customer's locations.
- **Qtn Validity, Rev.No, Rev Date, Subject, Attn** - Details carried onto the printed quotation.
- **Terms / Terms and Conditions** - Contractual text printed with the offer.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Sales Order
entries.content:
The **Sales Order** in **DIGITZ ERP** records a confirmed commitment to supply a customer.

### Purpose

To state what the customer has ordered, at what price and on what terms, and to track how much of that order has since been delivered or invoiced.

### How It Works

An order is raised for a **Customer** against a **Warehouse**, and records the customer's own purchase order through the mandatory **LPO No** and **LPO Date**. It may be created from a won **Quotation**, in which case the quotation is linked.

A Sales Order posts **nothing** — no stock movement and no ledger entry. Its effect is tracked through **Qty Sold** on each line, which is maintained as delivery notes and sales invoices are raised against the order. From those quantities the order's **Status** is derived:

- **Pending** - nothing has been delivered or invoiced against the order yet.
- **Partial** - at least one line has been supplied for less than it ordered.
- **Completed** - every line has been fully supplied.

Where a line has been supplied for **more** than was ordered, an excess-allocation warning is raised.

On submission the order also **remembers its pricing**: for each line, the rate is written back to the customer's entry in the item's Customer Prices table, dated with the order's posting date.

From a Sales Order the system can generate a **Delivery Note** or a **Sales Invoice**, each built only from the quantity still outstanding — the pending quantity is calculated as ordered quantity less quantity already sold. If nothing is pending, generation is refused. An order can also be **duplicated** into a new order carrying the same customer, terms, totals, and lines.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the order is for, with address, tax id, and balance shown.
- **LPO No / LPO Date** - The customer's own purchase order reference; both required.
- **Quotation** - The won quotation the order was created from.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are to be supplied from.
- **Items** - Ordered items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Qty Sold** - Quantity of each line already delivered or invoiced.
- **Status** - `Pending`, `Partial`, or `Completed`, derived from sold quantities.
- **Credit Sale / Credit Days / Payment Terms / Payment Mode** - The settlement arrangement.
- **Salesman** and **Ship To Location** - Attribution and delivery location.
- **Default Cost Center** - Costing dimension carried onto downstream documents.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Delivery Note
entries.content:
The **Delivery Note** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods leaving the warehouse for a customer.

### Purpose

To take goods out of stock at the point they are dispatched and recognise their cost, so that the stock position and cost of sales are correct whether or not the invoice has been raised.

### How It Works

A delivery note is raised for a **Customer** from a **Warehouse**, and is usually generated from a **Sales Order** — carrying the customer, terms, totals, and the outstanding lines across. Because a note can draw on more than one order, the **Sales Orders** table is rebuilt from the line references each time the document is saved, listing every order the delivery draws on.

On submission the delivery note does two things:

**Stock.** Each line is issued from the warehouse and written to the stock ledger in the item's base unit, valued at the item's current moving average rate.

**Accounts.** For the resulting cost of goods sold, the note **credits the Inventory account** and **debits the Cost of Goods Sold account**. Revenue, receivable, and tax are not posted here — they belong to the Sales Invoice.

As quantities are delivered, **Qty Sold** on the originating Sales Order lines is updated and each affected order's status is re-derived. The same happens in reverse when the note is cancelled or deleted.

The **Is Delivered** flag records that the goods have physically reached the customer, separately from the document having been submitted.

### Validations

- Stock must exist in the warehouse and be sufficient for the quantity being issued, unless the Company has **Allow Negative Stock** enabled.
- An item with no prior stock ledger entry must have a valuation rate on the Item master; otherwise the system stops with *"Please provide a valuation rate for the item, as there is no existing purchase invoice for it."*
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing delivery note; the system advances the posting time automatically and stops if no free slot is found.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the goods are delivered to, with address and balance.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are issued from.
- **Sales Orders** - The orders this delivery draws on, rebuilt from the line references.
- **Items** - Delivered items with quantity, unit, rate, and the reference to the order line.
- **Is Delivered** - Marks that the goods have reached the customer.
- **LPO No / LPO Date** - The customer's purchase order reference, carried from the order.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the note's stock and ledger postings.
- **Ship To Location** and **Salesman** - Delivery location and attribution.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Sales Return
entries.content:
The **Sales Return** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods taken back from a customer and reverses their financial effect.

### Purpose

To bring returned goods back into stock and unwind the original sale — reducing the receivable, the income recognised, the output tax, and the cost of goods sold.

### How It Works

A return is raised for a **Customer** into a **Warehouse**, and its lines reference the original **Sales Invoice** line being returned. The **Invoices** table records which invoices the return is set against.

On submission the return receives the goods back into the warehouse and posts the reversal to the general ledger:

- The **Accounts Receivable account is credited** with the rounded total, reducing what the customer owes.
- The **Income account is debited** with the value excluding tax.
- The **Tax account is debited** with the tax total, reversing the output tax.
- The **Inventory account is debited** and the **Cost of Goods Sold account credited** with the cost of the returned goods, so cost of sales is unwound at the same value it was recognised at.
- Any **round off** is posted to the round off account.

Where the return is not a credit sale, payment postings are made as well, so a return against a cash sale is settled immediately rather than sitting on the receivable.

The return also keeps the surrounding documents consistent: quantities on the originating **Sales Invoice** and **Delivery Note** lines are adjusted, any **Receipt Schedule** entries are rebuilt against the return, and the status of each affected **Sales Order** is re-derived.

### Validations

- The quantity returned cannot exceed what remains available on the original sales line. The check is cumulative — all other returns already raised against that line are counted, so a line cannot be over-returned across several documents.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the goods are returned from.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are received back into.
- **Items** - Returned items with quantity, unit, rate, and the reference to the original sales line.
- **Invoices** - The sales invoices the return is set against.
- **Credit Sale** - Determines whether the return reduces the receivable or settles immediately.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the return's stock and ledger postings.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Tab Sales
entries.content:
**Tab Sales** in **DIGITZ ERP** is a shorter entry screen for over-the-counter sales, where the full order-to-delivery cycle is unnecessary.

### Purpose

To record a sale in a single step, without raising a quotation, order, and delivery note first — while still producing the same accounting and stock effect as a normal sale.

### How It Works

Tab Sales has its own entry page and is filled in like a sales document: customer, warehouse, payment mode, and lines with quantity, unit, rate, and tax.

Behind it, the document maintains a **linked Sales Invoice**. As the Tab Sales record is built and saved, the corresponding Sales Invoice is created or brought back into step with it. When the Tab Sales document is submitted, that linked Sales Invoice is submitted with it — and the invoice, not the Tab Sales record, is what posts to stock and to the ledger.

This means the accounting behaviour of a counter sale is exactly that of a Sales Invoice, described under [Sales Invoice](#sales-invoice). Tab Sales is the faster way to reach it.

**Auto Save Delivery Note** additionally produces the delivery documentation for the sale where the goods are handed over at the same time.

### Validations

- Stock availability is checked for the items being sold, as it is on any document that issues stock.
- An item with no prior stock ledger entry must carry a valuation rate on the Item master.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing record.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the sale is made to.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are sold from.
- **Items** - Sold items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Credit Sale / Payment Mode / Payment Account** - How the sale is settled.
- **Auto Save Delivery Note** - Produces the delivery documentation alongside the sale.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Document Flow
entries.content:
The selling documents in **DIGITZ ERP** are connected by rules that decide which document may be raised from which, and what is still outstanding.

### Quotation to Sales Order

A **Quotation** must be marked **Won** before it can be converted; the system refuses to proceed otherwise. Conversion is only offered while the quotation is unused — once a Sales Order, Delivery Note, or Sales Invoice exists against it, it cannot be converted again. Where the quotation was raised against a **Prospect**, the system first checks that a Customer exists for that prospect.

### Sales Order onward

From a submitted Sales Order the goods can be recorded either through a **Delivery Note** first, or straight onto a **Sales Invoice**. In both cases only the **pending quantity** is carried over — ordered quantity less quantity already sold — and generation is refused when nothing is pending:

> *"No pending items in the Sales Order to generate a Delivery Note."*

The system tracks whether an order has already been taken down either route, so that a single order is not accidentally delivered and invoiced twice over for the same quantity.

Because the pending quantity drives everything, an order can be supplied across several deliveries or invoices, each drawing what remains. A single **Delivery Note** can likewise draw on more than one Sales Order, and the orders it draws on are listed on the note.

### Delivery Note to Sales Invoice

A **Sales Invoice** raised against delivered goods references the delivery notes it bills, so the same goods are not invoiced twice.

### Sales Return

A **Sales Return** is raised against **Sales Invoice** lines rather than against orders or deliveries, since it is the invoiced quantity that determines what may be returned. Returning goods adjusts the originating invoice and delivery note quantities and re-derives the status of every affected Sales Order.

### What each stage affects

| Document | Stock | General Ledger |
|---|---|---|
| Quotation | — | — |
| Sales Order | — | — |
| Delivery Note | Goods out | Inventory credited, Cost of Goods Sold debited |
| Sales Invoice | Goods out, when raised without a delivery note | Receivable, income, and tax |
| Sales Return | Goods in | Receivable credited; income, tax, and cost of sales reversed |

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Reports
entries.content:
The **Selling Reports** in **DIGITZ ERP** present the sales documents as registers, as itemwise detail, and as analysis.

### Registers

**Quotation Register**, **Sales Order Register**, **Delivery Note Register**, **Sales Register**, and **Sales Return Register** list the documents of each type over a period with their customer, dates, and values — the document-level view of what was quoted, ordered, delivered, invoiced, and returned.

### Itemwise detail and summaries

Each register has an itemwise pair. The **Itemwise Register** reports break the documents down to their individual lines, and the **Itemwise Summary Report** consolidates those lines by item:

- **Quotation Itemwise Register** and **Quotation Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Order Itemwise Register** and **Sales Order Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Delivery Note Itemwise Register** and **Delivery Note Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Itemwise Register** and **Sales Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Return Itemwise Register** and **Sales Return Itemwise Summary Report**

Use the register when a specific transaction must be traced, and the summary when the question is how much of an item was sold or returned in total.

### Daily activity

**Daily Report** and **Daily Report Detailed** present a day's selling activity, the detailed variant going down to the individual transactions behind the totals.

### Analysis

**Periodic Sales Analysis Report** presents sales across periods for comparison rather than for tracing individual documents.

**Sales Receipt Analysis Report** shows sales against what has been received, for reviewing the collection position.

**Customer Outstanding Summary Report** presents the balance owed per customer.

**Projectwise Billing Report** groups billing by project, for work sold and invoiced against a specific job.

**Top Customer Sales Report** and **Sales Chart - Top Customer Sales** rank customers by sales value, as a table and as a chart, giving a quick view of where revenue is concentrated.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Taxation Module Overview
entries.content:
The **Taxation Module** in **DIGITZ ERP** covers indirect tax — how a tax rate is defined, how it is applied to a transaction, which account it lands in, and how the period's position is reported for filing.

The module is deliberately small, because tax is not a separate process here. **Tax is calculated on the transaction that gives rise to it**, line by line, and posted to the ledger by that same transaction. There is no separate tax voucher and no month-end tax computation run. What the Taxation workspace provides is the **reporting layer** over what the operational documents already recorded.

Three things make up the module:

1. **Definition** — the **Tax** master holds a named rate and the account it posts to. Company-level settings decide whether tax applies at all and whether rates are quoted inclusive or exclusive of it.
2. **Application** — every sales, purchase and expense document computes tax per line from the item's tax and the document's inclusive/exclusive setting, and stores the taxable amount alongside the tax amount.
3. **Reporting** — three reports read those stored amounts: **Output Tax Report** (what was charged), **Input Tax Report** (what was borne), and **Consolidated Tax Report** (the net position, laid out for a UAE VAT return).

### Why it is built this way

Because the tax figure is stored on the document rather than derived at reporting time, the three reports are **reconciliations of records, not recalculations**. The Input Tax Report and the Consolidated Tax Report's *Standard Rated Expenses* line are built from the same query, so they cannot disagree with each other — the consolidated figure is by construction the sum of the rows the detail report lists.

Only **submitted** documents are counted. Drafts and cancelled documents never appear in a tax report.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Tax Setup
entries.content:
Tax configuration lives in two places: the **Tax** master, which defines a rate, and the **Company**, which decides how that rate is used.

### The Tax master

A **Tax** record is named by its **Tax Name**, which must be unique, and carries:

- **Tax Type** — `VAT` or `GST`
- **Tax Rate** — the percentage
- **Account** — the ledger account the tax posts to

One Tax record therefore ties a rate to an account. Items point at the Tax record they attract, and transactions copy the name and rate onto the line.

### Company tax settings

The **Company** holds the settings that govern the whole installation:

- **Tax ID** — the company's own registration number (TRN), printed on outgoing documents
- **Tax Type** — `VAT` or `GST`
- **Tax** — the default Tax record
- **Tax Account** — the account sales and purchase invoices post their tax to
- **Rate includes tax in sales transactions** — whether quoted rates are tax-inclusive by default
- **Tax not applicable for the company** — switches tax off entirely for the installation

### What a fresh installation starts with

Installation creates a working UAE VAT setup rather than leaving it blank:

- an account **UAE VAT @ 5 %** under **Duties & Taxes**, on the liability side
- a Tax record **UAE VAT - 5%**, type `VAT`, rate `5`, pointing at that account
- the company set to that Tax and that Tax Account, with **Tax not applicable** off and **Rate includes tax** off
- the generic items shipped with the system (`Advance Received`, `Generic Labour`, `Generic Material`) already carrying **UAE VAT - 5%**

So a new installation charges 5% VAT correctly from the first invoice, and changing the rate is a change to one master record.

### Suppressing tax

Tax can be switched off at three levels, each narrower than the last:

- **Company** — *Tax not applicable for the company*, which disables tax across the installation
- **Item** — *Tax Not Applicable* on the item, so that item never attracts tax
- **Line** — a line whose item has no Tax linked simply carries a zero rate

When the company-level switch is on, it overrides the item: no line picks up a tax rate regardless of what the item says.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — How Tax Is Applied
entries.content:
Tax is computed **per line**, when the document's totals are built, and the result is stored on the line and rolled up to the header. Nothing recalculates it later.

### What a line starts from

When an item is placed on a line, the system reads the **Tax** linked to that item and copies its **name** and **rate** onto the line. If the item is marked *Tax Not Applicable*, or the company has tax switched off, the line's tax name is cleared and its rate set to zero.

### Rates quoted excluding tax

This is the default. The rate is the pre-tax price, and tax is added on top of the discounted line value:

- **Taxable amount** = (quantity × rate) − line discount
- **Tax amount** = taxable amount × rate ÷ 100
- **Net amount** = taxable amount + tax amount
- **Gross amount** = quantity × rate

### Rates quoted including tax

When **Rate includes tax** is on, the quoted rate already contains the tax, and the tax is extracted out of it:

- **Tax amount** = (quantity × rate) × rate% ÷ (100 + rate%)
- **Rate excluding tax** = rate − (rate × rate% ÷ (100 + rate%))
- **Net amount** = (quantity × rate) − line discount
- **Gross amount** = net amount − tax amount

**Constraint:** the inclusive mode is not designed to be combined with **line-item discounts**. In inclusive mode the tax is extracted from the full quoted line value, so a line discount reduces the net amount without reducing the tax. Use bill-level discount, or quote rates exclusive of tax, where line discounts are needed.

### Taxable amount is recorded only where tax was charged

A line records a **taxable amount** when it actually bore tax. A line at a zero rate — an exempt or out-of-scope item — records a taxable amount of zero, not its value.

This is what makes the reports meaningful: the header's **Taxable Total** is the **standard-rated** value of the document, not its total value. It is that figure, and not the gross or net total, that the tax reports sum.

### Document totals

Each document then holds, in its own right:

- **Gross Total** — the pre-tax value of the lines
- **Total Discount in Line Items** — the discounts given on the lines
- **Taxable Total** — the standard-rated portion
- **Tax Total** — the tax charged or borne
- **Net Total** — the payable value, after bill-level discount

The tax reports read these stored header figures directly.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Tax Accounting
entries.content:
Every document that charges or bears tax posts that tax to the ledger itself, as part of its own posting. There is no separate tax journal.

### Sales side

A **Sales Invoice** splits its value in two when it posts:

- the income account is **credited** with the net total *less* the tax total
- the company's **Tax Account** is **credited** with the tax total
- the receivable account is **debited** with the full net total

The tax line is only written when there is tax to write. A wholly exempt invoice posts income and receivable alone.

### Purchase side

A **Purchase Invoice** mirrors it: the company's **Tax Account** is **debited** with the tax total, against the payable account.

So the same account carries output tax as a credit and input tax as a debit, and its balance is the net position — which is what the Consolidated Tax Report reports independently from the documents.

### Expense Entry and Additional Expense Entry

Expenses behave differently in one respect worth knowing: the tax on an expense row posts to **the account named on the Tax record used by that row**, not to the company's Tax Account.

Tax is grouped by **tax record and expense date**, and one debit is posted per combination, so an entry covering several dates or several tax rates produces one tax posting for each. Rows with no tax produce no tax posting at all.

### Credit Notes and Debit Notes

Credit and Debit Note lines carry their **own tax account** per row. The tax across the rows is grouped by account and posted as one entry per account — **debited** on a Credit Note (reversing output tax) and **credited** on a Debit Note (reversing input tax).

### The effect

Because tax posts with the transaction, the tax accounts in the trial balance and the tax reports are two views of the same events. A discrepancy between them is a data question about specific documents, not a reconciliation exercise.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Tax Registration Numbers
entries.content:
A compliant tax invoice has to show both parties' registration numbers, so the system carries them as data rather than as print-time typing.

### Where they are held

- **Company → Tax ID** — the business's own registration number
- **Customer → Tax Id** — the customer's number
- **Supplier → TRN No** — the supplier's number

### How they reach documents

The party's number is **fetched onto the transaction** when the party is selected, and carried forward as documents convert — a Quotation's number follows into the Sales Invoice, Sales Order and Delivery Note created from it.

Because it is stored on the document rather than looked up when printing, a document printed later shows the number that applied **when it was raised**, which is the correct behaviour if a party's registration subsequently changes.

### On printed output

The generated print for Quotations, Sales Invoices, Sales Orders, Delivery Notes and Purchase Orders carries the company's registration number and the counterparty's, alongside the tax breakdown the document computed.

### Emirate

**Customers and Suppliers also carry an Emirate** — one of the seven UAE emirates. On the customer it is not decorative: the Consolidated Tax Report groups standard-rated supplies by the customer's emirate, which is how the UAE VAT return requires them to be declared. A customer left without an emirate is reported under **Unknown**, so the figure is never lost, but it does have to be corrected before filing.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Output Tax Report
entries.content:
The **Output Tax Report** lists the tax charged to customers in a period, document by document.

### What it covers

Three document types, all submitted only:

- **Sales Invoice** — as recorded
- **Sales Return** — reported **negative**
- **Credit Note** — reported **negative**

Returns and credit notes therefore reduce the output tax rather than being listed as separate positive liabilities, so the column totals are the amounts actually due.

### Columns

**Invoice No · Voucher Type · Posting Date · Customer · Gross Total · Discount Total · Taxable Total · Net Total · Tax Total**

Having gross, discount, taxable and net side by side makes it possible to see *why* a document's taxable value differs from its face value — a discount, or a line that was not standard-rated.

### Filters

- **Customer** — a single customer
- **From Date / To Date** — the period, defaulting to the current month

### Chart

The report plots **Net Total** and **Tax Total** grouped by the **customer's emirate**, so the geographic split required for the return is visible before the consolidated report is opened. Customers with no emirate recorded are grouped under *Not Specified*.

### Reading it

Rows are ordered by posting date and then document number, which makes it usable as the working paper behind the return: the period reads in the order it happened, and the negatives sit where the credits were issued.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Input Tax Report
entries.content:
The **Input Tax Report** lists the tax borne on purchases and expenses in a period, document by document.

### What it covers

Five sources, all submitted only:

- **Purchase Invoice** — as recorded
- **Purchase Return** — reported **negative**
- **Debit Note** — reported **negative**
- **Expense Entry** — its rows aggregated per entry and supplier
- **Additional Expense Entry** — likewise

The two expense types matter: a great deal of recoverable input tax never passes through a purchase invoice at all, and a report that only read invoices would understate the claim.

### How expenses are treated

Expense rows carry their own supplier, date, tax and taxable amount, so an entry covering several suppliers is reported as **one row per supplier**, with its taxable and tax amounts summed. The entry's date is taken from the earliest expense date on the rows included.

A **Debit Note** is dated by its own date field rather than a posting date, and its net value is derived as taxable plus tax, because the document does not store a net total of its own.

### Columns

**Invoice No · Voucher Type · Posting Date · Supplier · Gross Total · Discount Total · Taxable Total · Net Total · Tax Total**

### Filters

- **Supplier** — a single supplier, applied to invoice and debit note headers and to expense rows by their own supplier
- **Voucher Type** — restricts the listing to one kind of document
- **From Date / To Date** — the period, defaulting to the current month

### Why it reconciles with the consolidated report

The rows are produced by the shared input tax source that the **Consolidated Tax Report** also uses for its *Standard Rated Expenses* line. The consolidated figure is the aggregate of exactly these rows, computed over the same query — so the detail always explains the summary, with no possibility of the two drifting apart.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Consolidated Tax Report
entries.content:
The **Consolidated Tax Report** is the report the tax return is prepared from. It takes a period and states the whole tax position in one statement — output tax on supplies, input tax on expenses, and the net amount payable or recoverable — laid out in the shape a UAE VAT return expects.

It is the last of the three tax reports: **Output Tax Report** lists what was charged, **Input Tax Report** lists what was borne, and the **Consolidated Tax Report** summarises both into the figures that are declared.

### Structure

The report is a single statement in three parts.

**1. Standard rated supplies, by emirate.** One line per emirate — *Standard rated supplies in Dubai*, and so on — showing the taxable total and the tax total of Sales Invoices, grouped by the **customer's** emirate. Sales Returns and Credit Notes are subtracted from the emirate they belong to, so each line is net of credits issued. **All seven emirates are always listed**, at zero if there was no activity, because a return needs every line stated. Supplies to customers with no emirate recorded appear under **Unknown**. A **Total** line closes the section.

**2. Standard Rated Expenses.** A single line for the whole input side — purchase invoices, purchase returns, debit notes and both kinds of expense entry — carrying the taxable total and the tax total.

**3. Consolidated Tax.** The closing line: output taxable and tax **less** input taxable and tax. Its tax figure is the net position for the period — payable when positive, recoverable when negative.

### Filters

- **From Date / To Date** — the period, defaulting to the current month

### Columns

**Particulars · Taxable Total · Tax Total**

### How it relates to the other two reports

The consolidated report is a summary of the same records the detail reports list, not a separate calculation:

- its **supplies** lines aggregate what the **Output Tax Report** itemises
- its **Standard Rated Expenses** line is computed from the identical query behind the **Input Tax Report**

So the working papers for a return are the two detail reports, and the return itself is this one. If a consolidated figure looks wrong, the document that caused it is in the corresponding detail report for the same period — there is no intermediate computation to investigate.

### What to check before filing the Consolidated Tax Report

Run the Consolidated Tax Report before filing and review it for two things, because both are visible here and nowhere else:

- **Supplies reported under Unknown.** A customer whose emirate has not been recorded is still counted, but under *Unknown* rather than an emirate. Set the emirate on the customer and re-run the report, because a return cannot be filed with supplies in an emirate that does not exist.
- **An emirate showing a negative supplies figure.** Credits issued in the period exceeded invoices raised in it. This is legitimate — a credit note often follows the invoice into the next period — but it is worth confirming that the credit was intended before the figure is declared.

Checking the report before filing is the point at which both are cheap to fix. Once the return is submitted, correcting an emirate means an amendment rather than an edit.

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Overview
entries.content:
**Every Relationship — Nurtured with Intelligent CRM.**

DIGITZ CRM is a complete customer relationship and sales management system. It captures leads, qualifies them, converts them into deals, tracks every conversation along the way, and rolls won business up into revenue you can report on — all inside one governed system.

What makes DIGITZ CRM different is that it keeps **relationship building** and **deal making** as two distinct disciplines. Acquiring and qualifying a lead is not the same job as progressing a deal to a close, so each has its own pipeline, its own stages and its own working screen. Nothing is forced into a single mixed funnel.

### What You Can Do

- Maintain partner and customer relationships as **Associations**, with a full engagement history
- Capture and qualify **Leads**, with stage-by-stage tracking of how each relationship matures
- Convert qualified leads into **Opportunities**, with commercial guardrails that prevent premature conversion
- Run the day from a personal **Action Centre** — activities, planned work, task inbox and calendar
- See any lead or deal in a single pane with **360 views**, including a complete relationship timeline
- Track meetings, tasks, checklists and compliance documents against every record
- Roll won revenue automatically up to the Lead, the Association and the Strategy
- Measure your team with **KRA/KPI performance** records and over 30 built-in reports

### Who It Is For

- **Sales executives** — a personal daily working surface and a clear view of their own pipeline
- **Sales managers** — branch and team pipelines, conversion rates, activity levels and performance scoring
- **Business owners** — cross-funnel KPIs, revenue visibility by strategy, and audit-ready history

*Use the listing on the left to browse each area of the application.*

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Key Concepts
entries.content:
Understanding six ideas is enough to use DIGITZ CRM confidently.

### The Relationship Hierarchy

```
Strategy          how you go to market (e.g. Sales Process, Sales Partnership)
  └── Association   the relationship or partner account
        └── Lead      an acquisition and qualification record
              └── Opportunity   a deal you are trying to win
```

Every Lead belongs to an Association, and every Opportunity comes from a Lead. This chain is what allows won revenue to be reported at any level — a single deal, a whole relationship, or an entire go-to-market strategy.

### The Six Concepts

#### 1. Strategy

The highest level — how you approach the market. Two are provided out of the box: **Sales Process** (direct selling) and **Sales Partnership** (selling through partners). Revenue is summarised against each.

#### 2. Association

The relationship account: the company or partner you are dealing with. It carries contacts, engagement history, an association stage, an action plan and its own revenue summary. A **Default Association** is created for you, so you are never blocked when creating your first lead.

#### 3. Lead

An acquisition and qualification record — the company or person you are working to qualify. A Lead holds identity, contacts, ownership (branch, executive, distributor), and all the working detail: activities, meetings, tasks, checklist, documents and remarks.

#### 4. Opportunity

A deal. It must originate from a Lead and must list at least one product or service. It carries the commercial detail — probability of winning, expected closing date, competitors, quotation and order values, and the quote-to-invoice trail.

#### 5. Executive

Your salespeople are recorded as **Executives**, linked to a user account, a branch and optionally a distributor. The Executive record is what drives data access: it decides which leads, deals and activities a person sees, and which fields they may change.

#### 6. Stage

Both Leads and Opportunities move through stages. Stages are configurable — you can rename them, reorder them, or add your own — because the system never relies on the *name* of a stage. Instead every stage is classified by **type**, which is what the software actually acts on.

| Record | Stage types available |
| --- | --- |
| Lead | Open · Qualified · Nurturing · Disqualified · Inactive |
| Opportunity | Open · Won · Lost · On Hold |

### Benefits

- Your stage names can match how your business actually speaks, without breaking any reporting
- Revenue is meaningful at every level of the hierarchy, not just per deal
- Access control follows your real organisation — branches, distributors and executives

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Setting Up
entries.content:
### Overview

DIGITZ CRM installs with a working set of master data, so you can start entering leads immediately. This section covers what is created for you and what you should configure before rolling out to a team.

### What Is Created Automatically

On installation the system creates:

| Master | Seeded values |
| --- | --- |
| Lead Stages | New · Contact Attempted · Contacted · Engaged · Qualified · Nurturing · Disqualified · Inactive |
| Opportunity Stages | New Opportunity · Discovery · Requirement Confirmed · Solution Proposed · Quotation Sent · Negotiation · Approval Pending · Verbal Commitment · Won · Lost · On Hold |
| Association Stages | New Association · Contacted · Exploring Synergies · Onboarding · Active Partnership · Inactive |
| Strategies | Sales Process · Sales Partnership |
| Association | Default Association |
| Activity Types | Call · Email · Online Meeting · Physical Meeting · WhatsApp · Task |
| Sales Effort Target Types | Sales Conversion / Proposals / Activities per month |
| Project Execution Milestones | Milestone 1 – 8 |
| KRA Group | Default KRA Group |

### Recommended Setup Order

#### 1. Branches

Create a Branch for each office or location. Branches carry address, currency and contact details, and are the primary way data is partitioned between teams.

#### 2. Distributors and Business Partners

If you sell through distributors, create them and assign each to a branch. The first distributor created for a branch automatically becomes that branch's default.

#### 3. Executives

Create one Executive per salesperson and link it to their user account, their branch, and — where relevant — their distributor. This single step configures their data access: the system automatically restricts that user to their branch and grants access to their distributor.

#### 4. Product Portfolio

List the products and services you sell. Every Opportunity must reference at least one, and product-wise revenue reporting depends on this list.

#### 5. Review Your Stages

Rename or reorder the seeded stages to match your sales process. Two settings matter most:

- **Sequence** — controls the order that stages appear in the pipeline boards
- **Allows Opportunity Creation** — marks the lead stages from which a deal may be created (by default, only *Qualified*)

#### 6. Checklist Templates

Create a CheckList Task Template of the steps that should be completed on every lead or every opportunity, and mark it as the default. New records will pick it up automatically.

#### 7. CRM Settings

Finally, review the CRM Settings screen to switch on the field rules your business needs — see [CRM Settings](#settings).

### Benefits

- A usable system from day one, with no blank-screen setup
- Access control configured as a by-product of recording your team, not as a separate exercise
- Stage names and sales steps that match how your business already works

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Associations
entries.content:
### Overview

An **Association** is the relationship account — the company, partner or institution you deal with. It sits above leads, so every lead you create is anchored to a relationship rather than floating on its own.

### Purpose

Associations let you:

- Keep one authoritative record of a company you deal with repeatedly
- See the total engagement history of a relationship, not just individual leads
- Track partner relationships through their own lifecycle stages
- Report revenue by relationship as well as by deal
- Record referral chains — which association introduced which

### How It Works

Each Association holds:

| Area | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Name, company, rank, market segment, industry, website |
| Contact | Primary contact plus a full contacts table |
| Address | Address lines, emirate, country |
| Relationship | Association stage, strategy, referred-by association |
| Ownership | Branch, sales executive, currency |
| Engagement | Activities and planned schedules |
| Planning | An action plan table with feedback and rating per action |
| Revenue | Fiscal-year revenue rolled up from won deals |
| Counters | Opportunity count and closed deal count |

Associations move through their own stages — from **New Association**, through **Contacted** and **Exploring Synergies**, to **Onboarding** and **Active Partnership**, or to **Inactive**.

### Key Features

#### 1. Relationship-First Structure

Because every lead must belong to an association, you always know which relationship a piece of business came from.

#### 2. Create a Lead Directly

A lead can be created straight from an association — identity, contacts and address are all copied across, so nothing is retyped.

#### 3. Referral Tracking

The *referred association* field records who introduced whom, letting you see which partners actually generate business.

#### 4. Revenue Summary

Won deals roll up automatically into the association's fiscal-year revenue table.

### Benefits

- One place to understand everything happening with a company
- Partner performance becomes measurable, not anecdotal
- Repeat business is visible rather than scattered across unrelated leads

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Leads
entries.content:
### Overview

A **Lead** is the acquisition and qualification record — the organisation you are working to turn into a customer. It is the busiest record in DIGITZ CRM and holds everything your team does before a deal exists.

### Purpose

The Lead record exists to answer three questions at any moment:

1. Who is this, and who owns them?
2. How far have we got in qualifying them?
3. What has actually been done, and what is planned next?

### How It Works

A Lead is created from scratch, from an Association, or from a Prospect record. It is named after the lead name, and requires an association, a branch and a country.

Information is organised into these areas:

| Area | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Lead name, company name, rank, lead stage, remarks |
| Primary contact | Contact person, designation, phone, mobile, email, WhatsApp |
| Contacts | A table of every other person at the organisation |
| Address | Address lines, emirate, country, website |
| Segmentation | Market segment, industry, campaign |
| Ownership | Branch, sales executive, distributor, partner type, currency |
| Qualification | Lead stage, first client visit date |
| Working tabs | Activities, schedules, meetings, meeting tasks, checklist, tasks, documents, remarks |
| Revenue | Fiscal-year revenue rolled up from won deals |

### Key Features

#### 1. Ownership Is Enforced, Not Suggested

When the person creating a lead is a registered Executive, their branch is applied automatically and cannot be changed to another branch. Distributor-funded executives cannot change the distributor, and once a sales executive is set on a lead, it is locked. This keeps territory and ownership honest.

#### 2. Settings-Driven Mandatory Fields

Whether contact name, mobile number, email, distributor or executive are mandatory is a configuration choice — see [CRM Settings](#settings). You enforce the discipline your business needs without customisation.

#### 3. First Client Visit Control

Where the setting is enabled, a lead cannot progress past its initial stage — or be converted into a deal — until the first client visit date is recorded. This makes "we actually met them" a real gate rather than a hope.

#### 4. Complete Working History

Every call, meeting, planned activity, task, checklist item, document and remark lives on the lead, and appears on the [Lead 360](#lead-360) timeline in date order.

#### 5. Automatic Checklist

If you have configured a default checklist template for leads, new leads pick it up automatically so no qualification step is skipped.

### Benefits

- One record that answers "where are we with this?" without asking anyone
- Territory and ownership rules that cannot be worked around
- Qualification discipline enforced by the system, not by memory

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Lead Stages & Qualification
entries.content:
### Overview

Lead stages describe how far a relationship has matured through **qualification**. They are fully configurable — you can rename them, reorder them, disable them, or add your own.

### How It Works

Every Lead Stage carries configuration that tells the system how to treat it:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Stage Type** | Classifies the stage as Open, Qualified, Nurturing, Disqualified or Inactive |
| **Sequence** | The order the stage appears in the pipeline board |
| **Allows Opportunity Creation** | Whether a deal may be created from a lead sitting in this stage |
| **Is Terminal** | Marks the stage as an end point for the qualification pipeline |
| **Disabled** | Removes the stage from selection on new records |

Because reporting is driven by **stage type** and not by stage names, you can rename "Qualified" to "Sales Accepted" — or to a term in your own language — and every KPI, board and report keeps working.

### The Standard Qualification Path

| Stage | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New | Open | Just captured, no contact yet |
| Contact Attempted | Open | We have tried to reach them |
| Contacted | Open | We have spoken to them |
| Engaged | Open | A real two-way conversation is under way |
| **Qualified** | **Qualified** | Fit, need and intent confirmed — **deals may be created from here** |
| Nurturing | Nurturing | Genuine but not ready — keep warm |
| Disqualified | Disqualified | Not a fit; end of the pipeline |
| Inactive | Inactive | Gone quiet; end of the pipeline |

### Key Features

#### 1. Qualification Gate

Only stages marked *Allows Opportunity Creation* can produce a deal. If someone tries to convert a lead too early, the system explains which stages allow it. This is what stops unqualified enquiries entering your pipeline as deals.

#### 2. Stage History

Every stage change is recorded with who moved it, when, from where, and how long the lead spent in the previous stage. This is what powers *days in stage*, qualification time and stagnation reporting.

#### 3. Change Reasons

When a stage is changed from a 360 view, a reason can be captured alongside it — particularly useful for disqualification analysis.

#### 4. Safe Stage Renaming

Older or ambiguous stages can be marked as *legacy*: existing records stay perfectly readable, but nobody can select the stage on new work. Any record left on a legacy stage is gathered into a **⚠ Stage Review** column on the pipeline board rather than quietly disappearing.

### Benefits

- Your pipeline speaks your language without breaking your reports
- Deals only enter the pipeline once a lead is genuinely qualified
- You can see exactly where leads slow down, with real elapsed time

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Opportunities
entries.content:
### Overview

An **Opportunity** is a deal you are working to win. It always originates from a Lead and must list at least one product or service.

### Purpose

Where the Lead answers "should we pursue this?", the Opportunity answers "will we win it, for how much, and when?".

### How It Works

An Opportunity is created by converting a qualified lead — see [Converting a Lead](#lead-conversion). It is named by its title, or by the project name where that setting is enabled.

| Area | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Title, ranking, originating lead, project name |
| Ownership | Branch, sales executive, distributor, currency |
| Deal qualifiers | Probability of winning, expected closing date, lead source, campaign, tender/project type |
| Products | One or more product/service lines with expected revenue |
| Competition | Competitors in the deal, special price flag and justification |
| Won financials | Won order value, converted date, earned revenue, revenue on hold |
| Project details | Quotation number/value/date, sales order, customer PO, invoice number and date |
| Working tabs | Activities, schedules, meetings, meeting tasks, checklist, tasks, remarks |

### Key Features

#### 1. Product-Led Value

Deal value comes from the product lines, not a single typed number. Your expected pipeline is therefore always the sum of real product revenue, and product-wise conversion reporting works without extra effort.

#### 2. Weighted Pipeline

Each deal carries a **Probability of Winning** (0–100%). Expected revenue multiplied by that probability gives the weighted pipeline shown on the dashboards — a far more honest forecast than raw pipeline value.

#### 3. Financial Guardrails

The system enforces the arithmetic for you:

- Probability of winning must be between 0 and 100
- A deal marked **Won** must carry a real order value
- Earned revenue can never be negative, nor exceed the won order value
- Revenue on hold is calculated as won order value minus earned revenue

#### 4. Quote-to-Invoice Trail

Quotation, sales order, customer PO and invoice details are recorded on the deal and appear as milestones on the [Opportunity 360](#opportunity-360) timeline, so commercial execution is visible in the same place as the selling.

#### 5. Competitor Tracking

Record which competitors are in each deal, and — where you had to discount — the special price and the reason for it.

### Benefits

- Forecasts based on product-level value and real probability
- Financial errors caught at entry rather than at month end
- One trail from first conversation to invoice raised

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Opportunity Stages & Deal Progression
entries.content:
### Overview

Opportunity stages describe how a **deal** progresses toward a close. They are configured separately from lead stages, and never mixed with them.

### How It Works

Each Opportunity Stage carries a **Stage Type** — Open, Won, Lost or On Hold — plus a sequence and a terminal flag. All deal reporting keys off the type, so the stage names remain yours to choose.

### The Standard Deal Path

| Stage | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New Opportunity | Open | Deal created |
| Discovery | Open | Understanding the requirement |
| Requirement Confirmed | Open | Scope agreed with the customer |
| Solution Proposed | Open | Our solution presented |
| Quotation Sent | Open | Commercials issued |
| Negotiation | Open | Price and terms under discussion |
| Approval Pending | Open | Awaiting customer sign-off |
| Verbal Commitment | Open | Won in principle, paperwork pending |
| **Won** | **Won** | Order received — revenue counts from here |
| **Lost** | **Lost** | Deal lost |
| On Hold | On Hold | Paused, not lost |

### Key Features

#### 1. Won Means Revenue

Only deals in a stage of type **Won** contribute to won order value and to the revenue roll-up. This is what keeps revenue reporting trustworthy no matter how stages are renamed.

#### 2. Win and Loss Rates

Win rate is calculated as won deals divided by all closed deals (won plus lost), so open deals never distort the figure. Loss rate is reported alongside it.

#### 3. Stage History and Ageing

Every move is timestamped, giving you days-in-stage per deal, average sales cycle length, and a clear view of where deals stall.

#### 4. Overdue Detection

Any open deal whose expected closing date has passed is flagged as overdue on the boards and counted on the dashboards.

### Benefits

- Honest revenue reporting that does not depend on stage naming
- Win/loss analysis that excludes deals still in play
- Immediate visibility of deals that have gone quiet or slipped their date

entries.topic: Converting a Lead to an Opportunity
entries.entity: Converting a Lead to an Opportunity
entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Converting a Lead to an Opportunity
entries.content:
### Overview

Conversion is the moment a qualified relationship becomes a deal. DIGITZ CRM treats it as a controlled step with commercial guardrails, not a simple copy.

### How It Works

Conversion can be started from the Lead form or from the [Lead 360](#lead-360) view. A popup opens pre-filled from the lead — title, ownership, contact details, currency, campaign, today's date and the default opening deal stage — and you complete the commercial detail and add the product lines.

### The Four Guards

Every conversion is checked against four rules, and the same rules apply no matter which screen you start from.

#### 1. The Lead Must Be Qualified

The lead's current stage must be one that allows opportunity creation. If it is not, the system names the stages that do, so the user knows exactly what to do next.

#### 2. First Client Visit

Where your organisation requires it, the first client visit date must be recorded before a deal can be created.

#### 3. Ownership Is Applied, Not Chosen

Branch, distributor and sales executive are taken from the converting user's own Executive record. They cannot be overridden during conversion, so a deal always lands in the right territory.

#### 4. A Deal Needs a Title and a Product

The opportunity title must be unique, and at least one product or service line must be present — the value of the deal comes from those lines.

### What Carries Across

| From the Lead | To the Opportunity |
| --- | --- |
| Lead name and record link | Originating lead and lead name |
| Branch, distributor, executive | Ownership (re-applied from the executive context) |
| Currency, campaign, remarks | Same fields |
| Contact person, mobile, email | Deal contact details |

The lead remains open and fully usable after conversion — one lead can produce several deals, and the [Lead 360](#lead-360) shows all of them along with a relationship indicator (*No Opportunity*, *One Open Opportunity*, *Multiple Open Opportunities*, *All Opportunities Closed*, or *Opportunity Won*).

### Benefits

- Only genuinely qualified business enters the deal pipeline
- No mis-assigned deals, because territory is applied by the system
- A single relationship can generate repeat business without losing its history

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — CRM Command Centre
entries.content:
### Overview

The **CRM Command Centre** is a concise cross-funnel snapshot: acquisition and qualification on one side, deal pipeline and revenue on the other. It is deliberately *not* a merged pipeline — the two disciplines are reported separately so neither hides the other.

### Purpose

It answers, in one screen, the questions a manager asks at the start of the day:

- Are we generating and qualifying enough new relationships?
- Is qualified work actually turning into deals?
- What is the pipeline worth, honestly weighted?
- What have we won?
- Is anything overdue?

### Key Metrics

| Metric | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| New Leads | Leads sitting in the initial stage |
| Qualified Leads | Leads that have reached a qualified stage |
| Qualified Without Opportunity | Qualified work nobody has converted — the most actionable number on the screen |
| Open Opportunities | Live deals |
| Lead-to-Opportunity Rate | Qualified leads that produced at least one deal, as a percentage of all qualified leads |
| Expected Pipeline | Total product value of open deals |
| Weighted Pipeline | Expected pipeline adjusted by each deal's probability of winning |
| Won Order Value | Value of deals in a Won stage |
| Overdue Closing | Open deals past their expected closing date |

### My Day

The Command Centre also carries a four-tile **My Day** panel — activities logged today, planned activities due today, tasks awaiting your response, and overdue tasks — which links through to the [Action Centre](#action-centre) where that work is actually done.

### Key Features

#### 1. Everything Is Permission-Aware

Every figure is calculated from the records you are allowed to see. An executive sees their own numbers; a manager sees their team's. Nobody has to be given extra access just to view a dashboard.

#### 2. Definitions Are Stated

Rate metrics show their numerator and denominator, so there is never a debate about how a percentage was calculated.

### Benefits

- One screen that separates relationship health from deal health
- Immediate sight of qualified work that is being left on the table
- Forecast figures that reflect probability, not optimism

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — CRM Action Centre
entries.content:
### Overview

The **CRM Action Centre** is the personal daily working surface — where an executive plans and executes their day. Everything on it is personal to the signed-in user.

### How It Works

The page opens on today, with a forward horizon (14 days by default) and an optional filter by record type. Five tabs organise the day:

| Tab | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Calendar** | Planned activities and dated tasks laid out by date |
| **Activities** | What was actually logged on the selected date |
| **Schedules** | Planned activities from the selected date across the horizon |
| **Task Inbox** | Tasks assigned to you awaiting acceptance |
| **My Tasks** | Tasks you have accepted or started |

Counts appear on each tab, and overdue work is highlighted.

### Key Features

#### 1. Truly Personal

Nothing on this page is shared. Filters live in the page and identity comes from your session, so two people using the Action Centre at the same time can never affect each other's view.

#### 2. Task Inbox with Accept and Reject

Tasks raised in meetings or assigned directly arrive in your inbox. You can **Accept**, **Reject** (a reason is required), **Start**, put back on **Hold**, or mark **Completed**. Status flows straight back to the meeting and the parent lead or deal.

#### 3. One Click to the Record

Every activity, schedule and task links directly to the relevant Lead 360 or Opportunity 360 view, so acting on an item never means hunting for the record.

#### 4. Managers Can Look, Not Interfere

A manager or administrator can view another user's day — or everyone's — to plan coverage. Even then, the task inbox stays personal: you can only accept or reject tasks assigned to you.

### Benefits

- Every executive starts the day with a single, honest list of what to do
- Commitments made in meetings cannot be quietly dropped
- Managers can see workload and coverage without disturbing anyone's queue

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Lead Development
entries.content:
### Overview

**CRM Lead Development** is the working screen for acquisition, engagement and qualification. It presents your leads as a board, with the KPIs that describe the health of the top of the funnel.

### How It Works

The page has three parts:

1. **KPI strip** — new leads, active leads, qualified leads, qualified-without-opportunity, opportunities generated, lead-to-opportunity rate, leads requiring stage review, and the won value associated with your leads
2. **Qualification board** — one column per lead stage, in your configured order
3. **Explorer** — a searchable, paged list for when you know what you are looking for

The columns are **lead stages only**. Deal stages never appear here.

### What Each Card Shows

| On the card | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Lead or company name | Identification |
| Rank | Your rating of the lead |
| Branch and executive | Ownership |
| Contact and mobile | Immediate action |
| Campaign | Where it came from |
| Age in days | How long since capture |
| **Days in current stage** | Real elapsed time — the stagnation signal |
| Opportunity count | Whether it has produced deals |
| Relationship indicator | *No Opportunity* · *One Open Opportunity* · *Multiple Open Opportunities* · *All Opportunities Closed* · *Opportunity Won* |

### Key Features

#### 1. Stagnation Is Visible

Days-in-stage is measured from the real stage-change history, not from the last time somebody saved the record — so a lead that has been sitting untouched for six weeks cannot be disguised by a minor edit.

#### 2. Stage Review Column

Any lead on a retired or ambiguous stage is collected into a **⚠ Stage Review** column, so cleanup work is visible instead of invisible.

#### 3. Relationship Context

The relationship indicator tells you at a glance whether a lead has ever produced business — the difference between a promising name and a proven relationship.

### Benefits

- The top of the funnel at a glance, per stage
- Immediate sight of leads going cold
- Qualified leads with no deal attached are impossible to miss

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Opportunity Deal Management
entries.content:
### Overview

**CRM Opportunity Deal Management** is the working screen for deal progression, commercial execution and revenue. It mirrors the Lead Development board, but for deals.

### How It Works

The page presents:

1. **KPI strip** — open deals, expected pipeline, weighted pipeline, quoted value, overdue closings, win rate, loss rate, won order value, earned revenue and revenue on hold
2. **Deal board** — one column per opportunity stage, in configured order
3. **Explorer** — searchable, paged deal list

Columns are **deal stages only** — lead qualification stages never appear here.

### What Each Card Shows

| On the card | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Deal title | Identification |
| Originating lead | Where it came from |
| Ranking | Deal priority |
| Branch and executive | Ownership |
| Expected value | Total product value |
| **Weighted value** | Expected value × probability of winning |
| Probability of winning | Confidence |
| Closing date + overdue flag | Timing risk |
| Age in days and days in stage | Momentum |

### Key Features

#### 1. Weighted Forecasting on the Card

Every deal shows both its full value and its weighted value, so a board full of large, low-probability deals reads honestly.

#### 2. Overdue Deals Are Flagged

Open deals past their closing date are marked on the card and counted in the KPI strip.

#### 3. Revenue Position at a Glance

Won order value, earned revenue and revenue on hold sit together, showing not just what was won but what has actually been realised.

### Benefits

- A forecast you can defend, deal by deal
- Slipping deals surface immediately
- Commercial execution measured alongside selling

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Lead 360
entries.content:
### Overview

**CRM Lead 360** shows everything about one lead in a single, fully interactive pane — and lets you work on it without opening the underlying form.

### How It Works

The page opens with a header (identity, stage, ownership, relationship indicator) and a set of tabs:

| Tab | What you do there |
| --- | --- |
| **Details** | View and edit the lead profile — rank, ownership, segmentation, dates and remarks |
| **Activities** | Log what happened: type, date/time, outcome |
| **Schedules** | Plan what is next, and mark it executed |
| **Meetings** | Record meetings with agenda and minutes, and raise tasks from them |
| **Meeting Tasks** | A read-only roll-up of every task raised in every meeting on this lead |
| **Checklist** | Work through the qualification checklist, with live progress |
| **Tasks** | General tasks assigned to executives |
| **Documents** | Compliance documents with expiry tracking |
| **Remarks** | Time-stamped narrative notes |

Alongside the tabs you see related opportunities with their stages and won value, and checklist progress.

### The Relationship Timeline

Every event on the lead is normalised onto a single timeline in date order: lead created, every stage change, activities, planned schedules, meetings, meeting tasks, general tasks, remarks — and the milestones of related deals, including when each was created, won or lost.

This is the fastest way to answer "what has actually happened with this account?" before a call.

### Key Features

#### 1. Change the Stage With a Reason

The stage can be moved directly from the page, with an optional reason recorded in the stage history. Only valid, enabled stages are offered.

#### 2. Full Editing, Same Rules

Adding a meeting or editing the profile here applies exactly the same validation and ownership rules as the standard form. Fields you are not permitted to change are shown greyed out — and the restriction is enforced on the server as well.

#### 3. Convert From Here

The conversion popup can be launched from Lead 360, with the same four guards described in [Converting a Lead](#lead-conversion).

### Benefits

- Complete account context before every conversation
- Day-to-day updates without navigating between forms
- A defensible audit trail of how a relationship developed

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Opportunity 360
entries.content:
### Overview

**CRM Opportunity 360** is the deal equivalent of Lead 360 — one interactive pane covering the commercial position, the working history and the delivery trail of a single deal.

### How It Works

The header carries deal identity, stage, ranking, originating lead and ownership. A financial summary sits alongside it:

| Figure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Expected pipeline | Total value of the product lines |
| Weighted | Expected value × probability of winning |
| Quoted value | Value of the quotation issued |
| Won order value | Order value once the deal is won |
| Earned revenue | How much of that has been realised |
| Revenue on hold | Won order value minus earned revenue |

### The Tabs

| Tab | What you do there |
| --- | --- |
| **Details** | Deal identity, qualifiers and commercial summary |
| **Activities** / **Schedules** | Log and plan engagement on the deal |
| **Meetings** / **Meeting Tasks** | Meetings, minutes and the commitments raised in them |
| **Checklist** | Deal checklist with live progress |
| **Tasks** | General tasks assigned to executives |
