| **Remarks** | Time-stamped narrative notes |
| **Project Details** | Quotation, sales order, customer PO and invoice details |

### The Deal Timeline

Every event is normalised in date order: deal created, every stage change, activities, schedules, meetings, tasks and remarks — plus commercial milestones for quotation, customer PO and invoice.

### Key Features

#### 1. Products and Competitors Together

Product lines and their expected revenue sit beside the competitors in the deal, so the value and the fight for it are visible at once.

#### 2. Quote-to-Invoice in the Same Place

Project details are edited on the same page, and appear as milestones on the timeline — no separate system to check whether the invoice was raised.

#### 3. Stage Moves With Reasons

As on Lead 360, the stage can be changed directly with a reason recorded — particularly valuable for loss analysis.

### Benefits

- The complete commercial picture of a deal on one screen
- Selling and delivery visible together
- A clear record of why a deal was won or lost

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Activities & Schedules
entries.content:
### Overview

Activities and schedules are how engagement is recorded in DIGITZ CRM. They apply to Leads, Opportunities and Associations alike.

### The Difference Between Them

| | **Activity** | **Schedule** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answers | What happened | What is planned |
| Records | Activity type, date & time, outcome | Activity type, date & time, expected outcome |
| Also carries | — | An *executed* flag |

Activity types are master data — Call, Email, Online Meeting, Physical Meeting, WhatsApp and Task are provided, and you can add your own.

### How It Works

An executive plans work as schedules, which then appear on their [Action Centre](#action-centre) calendar. As work is done, activities are logged with their outcome, and schedules are marked executed. Both appear on the record's 360 timeline.

### Key Features

#### 1. Planned Versus Actual

Because planning and execution are separate records, activity reporting can compare what was intended with what was delivered — the basis of the activity tracking reports and the sales effort targets.

#### 2. Personal Work Stays Visible

An executive always sees the work they personally planned or logged, even if the underlying record is later reassigned to a colleague. Organisational limits — branch and distributor — still apply.

#### 3. Association Engagement

Because associations carry their own activities and schedules, partner engagement is measurable even before a specific lead exists.

### Benefits

- Effort becomes measurable, not just outcomes
- Planned work turns into a real calendar
- Nothing an executive planned disappears from their own view

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Meetings & Tasks
entries.content:
### Overview

Meetings in DIGITZ CRM are not just diary entries — they are where commitments are created. Every task raised in a meeting is tracked to completion.

### How It Works

A meeting is recorded against a Lead or an Opportunity with its title, date, type (Internal or External), agenda and minutes. Within the meeting you raise **tasks**, each with a title, description, due date and an assigned Executive.

Those tasks then appear in two places:

1. In the assignee's **Task Inbox** on the [Action Centre](#action-centre)
2. In a read-only **Meeting Tasks** roll-up on the parent lead or deal, so anyone looking at the record sees every commitment made across every meeting

### The Task Lifecycle

```
Pending ──accept──► Accepted ──start──► Started ──► Completed
   ▲                    │
   └──── hold ──────────┘

Pending ──reject──► Rejected   (a reason is required)
```

General tasks — those raised outside a meeting — follow exactly the same lifecycle and appear in the same inbox.

### Key Features

#### 1. Tasks Are Assigned to Executives

Assignment is to a person in your sales structure, not to an anonymous user account, so task reporting lines up with performance reporting.

#### 2. Acceptance Is Explicit

A task is not "assumed" — the assignee must accept it, or reject it with a reason. Nothing sits in an ambiguous state.

#### 3. Status Flows Both Ways

Updating a task from the Action Centre updates the meeting and the parent record's roll-up automatically, so the record always tells the truth.

#### 4. Overdue Visibility

Tasks past their due date are counted and highlighted on the Action Centre and the Command Centre's My Day panel.

### Benefits

- Meeting outcomes turn into tracked commitments, not forgotten notes
- Every executive has one clear queue of accepted work
- Managers can see, per record, exactly what was promised and by whom

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Checklists
entries.content:
### Overview

Checklists ensure that every lead and every deal follows the steps your business considers non-negotiable.

### How It Works

You create a **CheckList Task Template** listing the steps — for example *Verify contact details*, *Initial call*, *Site visit*, *Proposal prepared* — and mark it as the default for leads, for opportunities, or both.

New records pick up the default template automatically. Each item is then ticked off as it is completed, and the 360 views show live progress (for example, *4 of 7 complete*).

### Key Features

#### 1. Separate Defaults for Leads and Deals

Qualification steps and deal-progression steps are rarely the same, so each has its own default template.

#### 2. Applied Automatically, Changeable Manually

The default is applied to new records without anyone remembering to do it, and a different template can be applied to an individual record when needed.

#### 3. Progress Is Visible

Checklist completion appears on the 360 views, giving an instant read on whether the process was actually followed.

### Benefits

- Consistent sales process across every executive and branch
- New team members follow the right steps from day one
- Process compliance becomes measurable

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Documents & Expiry
entries.content:
### Overview

Leads carry a **Documents** table for the paperwork a relationship depends on — trade licences, registrations, agreements, certificates and identification.

### How It Works

Each document row records:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Document Type | Selected from your Master Document Type list |
| Document | The attached file |
| Expiry Date | When it ceases to be valid |
| Status | Valid or Expired |

### Key Features

#### 1. Past Expiry Dates Are Rejected

A document cannot be filed with an expiry date already in the past — the record is stamped **Valid** when accepted.

#### 2. Automatic Daily Expiry Check

A scheduled job runs every day and flips any document whose expiry date has passed to **Expired**, so the status is always current without anyone maintaining it.

#### 3. Your Own Document Types

The Master Document Type list is yours to define, so the same structure works for any industry or jurisdiction.

### Benefits

- Compliance documents held against the relationship they belong to
- Expiries surface automatically instead of being discovered too late
- One consistent document vocabulary across the business

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Tracking Remarks
entries.content:
### Overview

**Tracking Remarks** are time-stamped narrative notes available on both Leads and Opportunities — the running commentary of a relationship or a deal.

### How It Works

Each remark carries a reference (what it relates to), the remark text, and a timestamp recording when it was written. The timestamp is set once, when the remark is created, and is never rewritten — so the sequence of events stays honest however the record is edited afterwards.

Remarks appear on the 360 timelines alongside activities, meetings and stage changes.

### Purpose

Remarks capture what structured fields cannot:

- Why a customer hesitated
- What a competitor is offering
- Internal context for a pricing decision
- Anything a colleague picking up the account should know

### Benefits

- Context survives people changing roles or leaving
- A defensible history of decisions and conversations
- Narrative and structured data on one timeline

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Revenue Roll-Up
entries.content:
### Overview

DIGITZ CRM automatically summarises won business up the relationship hierarchy, so revenue can be reported at any level without manual consolidation.

### How It Works

When a deal reaches a stage of type **Won**, its order value is attributed to a fiscal year (taken from the converted date) and rolled up:

```
Opportunity (Won)  →  Lead  →  Association  →  Strategy
```

Each of those records carries a fiscal-year revenue table that is rebuilt automatically whenever a deal is saved or removed. There is no month-end consolidation step and no chance of the totals drifting apart.

### Key Rules

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Only **Won** deals count | Pipeline is never mistaken for revenue |
| Fiscal year comes from the converted date | Revenue lands in the period it was actually won |
| Tables are rebuilt, not incremented | Totals cannot drift out of step over time |
| Deleting a deal recalculates the roll-up | Corrections flow through immediately |

### The Revenue Figures

| Figure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Expected Pipeline** | Total product value of open deals |
| **Weighted Pipeline** | Expected pipeline adjusted by probability of winning |
| **Quoted Value** | Value of quotations issued on open deals |
| **Won Order Value** | Value of deals in a Won stage |
| **Earned Revenue** | How much of the won value has been realised |
| **Revenue on Hold** | Won order value not yet earned |

### Benefits

- Revenue by deal, relationship, partner or go-to-market strategy — with no extra work
- Forecast and actuals side by side, using the same definitions everywhere
- Corrections and cancellations reflected immediately

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Performance Management (KRA & KPI)
entries.content:
### Overview

DIGITZ CRM includes a structured performance framework so sales performance is scored against agreed measures rather than impressions.

### The Structure

```
KRA Group  →  Key Result Area  →  Key Performance Indicator  →  KPI Unit
```

- **Key Result Area (KRA)** — an area of responsibility, e.g. *New Business*, *Customer Retention*
- **Key Performance Indicator (KPI)** — a measure within that area, e.g. *New qualified leads*
- **KPI Unit** — how it is measured, e.g. count, percentage, currency

### Monthly KRA Performance

One record is maintained per person per month, holding:

| Field | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| User, month, year | Who and when |
| KRA / KPI lines | Target value, achieved value, current value, unit, weightage, remarks |
| Total weightage | Ensures the scorecard adds up correctly |
| Expected vs actual turnover | Commercial contribution |
| Overall performance rating | The summary score |
| Feedback | Manager's written assessment |

### Sales Effort Target

Alongside outcome-based KRAs, **Sales Effort Target** sets activity expectations per executive — for example proposals per month, activities per month, or conversions per month. Effort is then compared against those targets in the Sales Target Report.

### Key Features

#### 1. Weighted Scorecards

Each KPI carries a weightage, and the record tracks how much weightage is still to be allocated — so incomplete scorecards are obvious.

#### 2. Effort and Outcome Together

Activity targets sit alongside result targets, so a shortfall can be traced to either insufficient effort or poor conversion.

#### 3. Reporting Built In

The Monthly KRA Performance Report and the KRA Performance Chart present the scores across the team.

### Benefits

- Objective, agreed measures instead of subjective reviews
- Underperformance diagnosed as an effort problem or a conversion problem
- A monthly record that stands up in an appraisal conversation

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Execution & Delivery
entries.content:
### Overview

Winning the deal is not the end of the work. DIGITZ CRM includes a small set of execution tools that cover personal planning and post-sale delivery.

### Week Plan

A dated weekly plan holding the intentions for the week — each line with a description, a done flag and remarks. Simple, personal, and reviewable at the end of the week.

### Daily Work Area

A per-day execution log. Each task line records:

- The task
- Completion percentage
- A high-priority flag
- A self-satisfaction rating
- Remarks

The day itself is then rated, with written feedback — creating a habit of daily reflection that feeds naturally into monthly performance reviews.

### Project Execution

For deals that have been won, Project Execution tracks delivery:

| Area | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Linkage | Customer and originating opportunity |
| Dates | Expected and actual start/end, expected invoice and payment dates |
| Value | Total project value and withholding value |
| Status | Not Started · On Going · Invoice Raised · Payment Received |
| Progress | Completion percentage, entered and calculated |
| Milestones | Milestone lines with expected/actual dates, completion and remarks |

### General Tasks

Standalone tasks with a due date and status, for work that does not belong to a particular lead or deal.

### Benefits

- The handover from sale to delivery stays inside one system
- Cash milestones — invoice raised, payment received — tracked against the original deal
- Personal planning and reflection built into the daily routine

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Quick Finance
entries.content:

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Users, Roles & Data Access
entries.content:
### Overview

DIGITZ CRM controls who sees what through your real organisation structure — branches, distributors and executives — rather than through a separate permissions exercise.

### The Roles

| Role | Typical holder | Can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CRM Sales Executive** | Salesperson | Create and work their own leads and deals; cannot delete |
| **CRM Sales Manager** | Team or branch manager | Full access to the records in their scope; cannot delete |
| **CRM Global Admin** | CRM owner | Full access including delete |
| **System Manager** | System administrator | Full system access |
| **Business Development Executive** | Reporting user | Access to the operational sales and activity reports |

### How Data Access Is Decided

#### 1. Role Permissions

Roles set the baseline of what each group may do. Sales executives work on their own records; deletion is reserved for administrators.

#### 2. Ownership Filtering

A sales executive sees the leads and deals they own or that have been assigned to them — not the whole database.

#### 3. Branch and Distributor Scope

When you record someone as an **Executive** and link them to a user, branch and distributor, the system automatically restricts that user to their branch and grants access to their distributor. Move them to another branch and the old access is removed for you.

#### 4. Activity Visibility

Engagement records follow the same rules through their parent record, with one deliberate exception: an executive always keeps sight of activities and schedules they personally created, even if the record is later reassigned. Branch and distributor limits still apply.

#### 5. Field-Level Locks

Even within a record they can edit, an executive cannot:

- Move a lead to a different branch
- Change the distributor, if they are a distributor-funded executive
- Reassign the sales executive once one has been set

These restrictions apply on every screen, including the 360 views.

### Key Features

#### 1. Access Configured by Recording Reality

Creating an Executive record configures that person's access. There is no separate permission matrix to maintain in parallel.

#### 2. Consistent Across Every Screen

Dashboards, boards, 360 views, reports and the Action Centre all apply the same rules, so no screen ever leaks a record another screen would hide.

### Benefits

- Territory integrity that cannot be worked around
- Onboarding a salesperson is one record, not a permissions project
- Managers can be given analytics without exposing other branches

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — CRM Settings
entries.content:
### Overview

**CRM Settings** is a single configuration screen that adapts the application to your sales process without customisation.

### The Settings

| Setting | Effect when enabled |
| --- | --- |
| **Use project name as opportunity name** | Deals are named from the project name instead of the title — suited to project and tender businesses |
| **Include project details in opportunity** | Shows the quotation, sales order, PO and invoice section on deals |
| **Use lead name label as company name** | Copies the lead name into the company name automatically |
| **First client visit date mandatory in lead** | A lead cannot progress past its first stage, or be converted, until the visit date is recorded |
| **Contact person name mandatory in lead** | Contact name required on new leads |
| **Mobile no mandatory in lead** | Mobile number required on new leads |
| **Email id mandatory in lead** | Email required on new leads |
| **Distributor mandatory** | Every lead and deal must name a distributor |
| **Executive field mandatory** | Every lead and deal must name a sales executive |
| **Hide distributor field** | Removes the distributor field for organisations that sell direct |

### How to Use Them

Start with the minimum and tighten over time. The mandatory-field settings are the most effective way to raise data quality: switching on *mobile number mandatory* does more for your follow-up rate than any amount of training.

The first-client-visit setting is the strongest commercial control available — it makes a physical or virtual meeting a prerequisite for a deal entering the pipeline.

### Benefits

- The same product supports direct sales, distributor sales and project businesses
- Data quality rules enforced by the system rather than by supervision
- Changes take effect immediately, with no development work

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Overview
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Overview

## What the app does

| Area | In short |
|---|---|
| Documents | A **Tracked Document** is one document of one holder: its type, number, authority and dates. Document types say whether they apply to organisations or to people, and which holder types must have them. Required documents that are missing are shown as gaps. |
| Cycles | Each validity period of a document is a **Document Cycle**. Renewing closes the cycle and opens the next, so the history of every renewal, reminder and payment is kept. |
| Groups and people | Documents are grouped along **dimensions** you define, such as *Document category*, *Client category* or *Department*. Groups carry **managers** (who oversee) and an **assignee** (who does the work). Every document gets exactly one assignee and all its groups' managers, worked out automatically (chapter 9). |
| Notifications | Ten e-mail events: reminders before expiry, expired, waiting on the holder, renewed, assigned to you, waiting time over, reassign needed and a weekly summary for managers; each switched on or off per company, in one branded layout (chapter 4). |
| Services | Services sold to clients (monthly, quarterly, yearly, every two years or once) produce one **task** per billing period, with checklists copied from templates. |
| Front end | A portal at `/tracker/` and administration at `/tracker/admin/`, outside Desk. The portal shows organisations and people with their documents as folders and files; it also has the expiry list and calendar, services and client requests. Desk keeps the forms and lists for administrators. |

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Key Concepts
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Key Concepts

## Two kinds of holder

Every document belongs to one of two kinds of holder:

| Holder | Examples | Its documents |
|---|---|---|
| **Organisation** | our own company, each client, a supplier | Trade License, Establishment Card, Tenancy Contract (Ejari), insurance policies |
| **Person** | our staff, a client's people | Emirates ID, visa, driving licence, labour card |

A person always belongs to one organisation. Which kinds of organisation and person exist is configuration, not code. Each kind is a **Holder Type**, such as *Our company*, *Client*, *Staff* or *Client contact*, and a new kind (*Supplier*, *Landlord*) needs no development.

## Roles

| Role | Works with |
|---|---|
| Tracker Administrator (shown as **Global Administrator** in Users & roles) | everything in every company, including configuration (dimensions, holder types, authorities, designations), the Tracker Companies, add-ons, the AI file check and WhatsApp templates; grants Tracker Administrator |
| Company Administrator | everything in **their** company: its records (including deleting them), settings and notifications, add-on switches, **Users & roles**, document types and every group's people for the company |
| Document Manager | the documents of the groups they manage: add, edit, renew, reassign, **deactivate**; organisations and people (add, edit); the **catalogue**: document types (add, edit) and groups (add; edit the ones they manage, with their people; delete an unused one) |
| Document Assignee | the documents and cycles assigned to them: renew, follow up payments; **add documents** (proposed as their own assignee) |
| Service Manager | service records (create, edit), tasks of services they manage, requests and feedback |
| Service Executive | tasks assigned to them, or whose prerequisites are assigned to them |
| Client | a portal user of one or more organisations: sees their documents and services, raises Client Requests and Client Feedback |

*Document Assignee* was called *Document Executive* before model 3; users kept their access when it was renamed.

**Roles are per company** (since 5.7.0). Except Tracker Administrator and Client, a role is held **in a company**: on the person's employee record in that company's home organisation. Someone who works for two companies can be a Document Manager in one and only a Document Assignee in the other; every page, list and menu follows their roles in the selected company. Give and change them in **Administration → Users & roles** (`/tracker/admin/users`), open to Tracker Administrators and the company's Company Administrators:
- **Invite** a staff member: their user (a set-password e-mail) and employee record, with the roles you tick.
- **Change roles** for this company. Only a Tracker Administrator grants Tracker Administrator, and nobody removes their own administrator role.
- **Remove access** when someone leaves this company (their open work is reassigned; their other companies and their user are kept), and **Restore access**.

**Global and company administrators on a multi-company site** (since 5.13.0). Users & roles shows two kinds of administrator:
- **Global Administrators** (the *Tracker Administrator* role, stored on the user) run every company and the installation-wide settings. They are listed at the top of the page with the companies they work in. A Global Administrator adds one by e-mail (an existing user, or a new one who gets a set-password e-mail) and removes one with **Remove**; nobody removes themselves, so there is always an administrator left. Company Administrators see the list but cannot change it.
- **Company Administrators** run only the companies they are given. A Global Administrator gives them per company: **Change roles** opens a table with a row per company (**Member** and the five company roles), so one person can be Company Administrator of two companies and a Document Assignee in a third, all in one save. Unticking *Member* removes their access to that company. **Invite** shows the same table, with the selected company ticked, and a *Global Administrator* box. A Company Administrator still sees and changes only the selected company.

The page also lists the company's client portal users (managed on each organisation) and the **Recent changes**. Removing a role from a user in Desk takes it away in every company; adding one in Desk gives nothing until it is given in a company. On the upgrade to 5.7.0 each employee kept the roles their user had, in each of their companies.

**Deleting is for administrators.** Tracker Administrators delete anything; Company Administrators delete their company's records (and unused groups). Everyone else **deactivates**: a deactivated document is *Not tracked*, keeps its cycles and history, and can be reactivated. Every delete, deactivation, invitation, role change and access change is recorded in the **Tracker Audit Log**, shown in Users & roles → Recent changes; a deleted document's cycles and notification logs are also kept in Frappe's Deleted Documents.

**Tracker Administrator, not System Manager.** Frappe's *System Manager* is an administrator of the whole site, also of other apps such as DIGITZ ERP, so on its own it gives no rights in the tracker. The tracker's administrator role is **Tracker Administrator**. It is given automatically to the site's System Managers when the app is installed, when Frappe's setup wizard creates the first user of a new site, and on the upgrade to this version; after that, give it (or not) to each administrator yourself, in Users & roles. Administrator always has every right. A System Manager can still change any user in Desk, Tracker Administrator included: give System Manager only to the people who run the site. The tracker never grants or removes it.

The full matrix and the record-level rules are in `digitz_tracker/digitz_tracker/TECHNICAL.md`. To open Desk, users also need **Allow DIGITZ Desk Access** (digitz_ui).

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Quick Start
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Quick Start ## Tracker Companies (Administration → Company & settings) A site holds **one Tracker Company**: the business using the tracker, with its own settings. Branches, divisions and other entities are added as **organisations**, not as companies. On a new site with no company yet, a Tracker Administrator signing in sees **Create company** at `/tracker/company`: the company is created together with its **home organisation** (the company as a document holder, of holder type *Our company*), which Company & settings then shows. The company is edited at `/tracker/admin/settings`, where it can also be disabled. A site set up before this rule keeps all its companies, but cannot add more. Companies are disabled, never deleted. The page has tabs: **General** (home organisation, its country, the default country and the company's settings), **Notifications** (e-mail and WhatsApp), **Add-ons**, **AI file check** and, for Tracker Administrators, **All companies**. **Save settings** saves every tab at once, so you can move between tabs before saving. | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | **Company name** | Shown in the sidebar and the company chooser. | | **Home organisation** | The company itself as an Organisation (its trade licence, its staff). It is created with the company when left empty. Its **reminder recipients** receive the internal reminders, and its **people with a user are the company's employees**. A company has one home organisation, normally set once: the page shows it read-only, with its **country** (edited on the organisation). Only a Tracker Administrator can change it, with **Change home organisation…**: the page first lists who stops and who starts being an employee, the company roles removed, the documents and open cycles that move to the next valid assignee (or Unassigned) and the reminder recipients before and after, and asks you to confirm. The change is recorded in the audit log (Users & roles → *Recent changes*). | | **Expiring within (days)** | The threshold for *expiring soon* (empty or 0 means 45). | | **Reminder days before expiry** | Comma-separated, e.g. `30, 15, 7, 1`. The expiry day is always reminded. | | **Notifications** | One row per e-mail event: **On**, and its **template** (*Default (Tracker · …)* unless you choose another Email Template). See chapter 4. | | **Never assign a person's own document to them** | When ticked, someone holding a document (their own Emirates ID, say) is skipped as its assignee (chapter 9). | | **Assign service tasks automatically**, **Service records need an executive** | Shown only while the Services add-on is on for the company (Add-on: Services). | | **Add-ons** | Register optional add-ons with their activation code and switch them on for this company (chapter 5). | | **AI file check** | For the whole site, not per company: **Check uploaded files with AI** (on by default), the **Model** (default `gpt-5.5`), and where the OpenAI key comes from. The key itself is never shown (chapter 3). | **WhatsApp** (Company & settings → WhatsApp). To send notifications on WhatsApp: 1. In Desk → **WhatsApp Account**, add your Meta WhatsApp Business account (access token, URL `https://graph.facebook.com`, API version, phone number ID, business account ID, app ID). Set it **Active** and **Default outgoing**. 2. Click **Register WhatsApp templates**. The tracker's ten templates (named `dzt_…`) are submitted to Meta for review. 3. Meta reviews them, which takes from minutes to a day. Click **Refresh status** until they show **APPROVED**. 4. In the notifications table, tick **WhatsApp** for the events you want. Every event starts with WhatsApp off. 5. Add WhatsApp numbers, with the country code: on an organisation's reminder recipients (*WhatsApp number*), on users (*Mobile No*) and on persons (*Mobile*). **The OpenAI key** is not typed on this page. It is copied into *Tracker AI Settings* (encrypted) on installation and on every migrate, from: 1. the bench config: `bench set-config -g digitz_openai_api_key ` (and `digitz_openai_project_id ` if the key belongs to a project), then `bench --site migrate`. Other DIGITZ apps can use the same entry; 2. otherwise the **DIGITZ AI Nexus** app's *Nexus Settings*, when that app is installed on the same site. Without a key, files are saved as usual and marked *Not checked*; Home's readiness lists **AI file check** until a key is set or the check is switched off. ## Masters (Administration → Masters) The document masters are an explorer at `/tracker/admin/masters`. Tracker Administrators change all of them. Document Managers add and edit **document types**, add **groups**, and edit the groups they manage (with their managers and assignee in the selected company); group dimensions, holder types and the company settings stay with the Tracker Administrator. Service Managers can read them. | Master | Purpose | |---|---| | **Holder Type** | A kind of organisation or person. For each one:
  • its **primitive** (Organisation or Person), which cannot change once holders use it;
  • for person types, the organisation types its people **belong to**;
  • whether reminders go to the **holder's organisation**, and also to the **person**;
  • its **required documents**: the document types every holder of this type should have (missing ones show in the holder's **Missing** section). One holder type can list several countries' documents (Staff: Emirates ID and Visa for the UAE, Aadhaar Card and PAN Card for India); each holder is only asked for those of its own country, and the holder type shows them per country;
  • the sort order.
A Tracker Administrator can **Delete** a holder type that nothing uses, in any company: no organisations, people or documents of that type, and no document type, group dimension or other holder type that lists it. The button appears only then, after a confirmation. *Our company* and *Staff* are built in and cannot be deleted. A holder type that is in use can be disabled instead. An organisation holder type such as *Client* also has **Add organisation**, the same form as in the Register; the new organisation then opens in the Register. | | **Group Dimension** | A way of grouping documents. Each one has:
  • a **source**: the group comes from the *Holder* (department, account) or from the *Document Type* (category);
  • an **assignment priority**: lower is asked first for an assignee.
Every dimension can be browsed in the Document register under **By group** (chapter 3). | | **Document Group** | A value of a dimension (*HR*, *Identity & residency*), shared by all companies. **Per company** it has its **managers** (any number) and one optional **assignee**; the explorer shows and edits those of the selected company. A group can be deleted only when nothing uses it. | | **Document Type** | What a document is. It records:
  • whether it **applies to** organisations or people;
  • its **country**: only organisations of that country, and their people, get it. A new type starts with the default country; clear it for a document of *any country*, such as a passport;
  • whether its **upload is required**: the document's file (a scan or PDF) should be on file. A document without it is still saved, with a warning, and flagged *No file* (chapter 3);
  • whether it **has an expiry**, and its **validity**: a number with a unit, **Yearly** or **Monthly** (2 + Yearly = two years, 6 + Monthly = six months). Adding a document with only an issue date works out its expiry date from it, and **Renew** proposes the next expiry date;
  • its default authority and an optional assignee per company;
  • its group in each dimension sourced from the document type;
  • the holder types it is **required for**.
Required documents are one setting seen from both sides: adding *Trade License* to the *Client* holder type's required documents is the same as adding *Client* to Trade License's *required for*. *Required for*, *Required documents* and *People belong to* are tag lists: **+ Add** picks from a searchable list (only types of the right kind are offered), and **×** removes one. | | Authority | The issuing authority (ICP, DED, MOHRE …): **Masters → Authorities**. | | Tracker Designation | Job titles of people: **Masters → Designations**. | The service masters (Service, Tracker Task Template, Task Prerequisites Template) are under **Administration → Service masters** (chapter 5). ## Organisations and people They are added in the Document register (**Register** in the sidebar, `/tracker/documents`) by Document Managers: - **Add organisation**, in a holder type's folder; - **Add person** and **Edit organisation**, in an organisation's profile; - **Edit person**, in a person's profile. | Record | Holds | |---|---| | **Organisation** | name, holder type, **tracker company** (the selected one when added), **country** (the default country when added), contacts, its group per Holder-sourced dimension, **reminder recipients**, **portal users** (users with only the Client role) | | **Person** | full name, holder type, organisation, designation, contacts, optional **user** (a staff member's login), its group per Holder-sourced dimension | **Managers and assignees are employees.** An employee of a company is an enabled person of its home organisation with a **user**; one user may be an employee of several companies (a person in each). A group's managers must be employees with the Document Manager or Tracker Administrator role, and an assignee an employee with Document Assignee, Document Manager or Tracker Administrator, in the company concerned. Both are checked when saved. **Who may use a company:** staff use the companies they are employees of; Client users the companies of the organisations they are portal users of; Tracker Administrators every company. An organisation moves to another company only while it has no documents, services, requests or feedback; its people move with it. ## Countries Legal documents differ by country, so each **document type** and each **organisation** has a country. - **The default country** is the one chosen in Frappe's setup wizard when the site was installed (System Settings → Country). New organisations and document types start with it. To change it, change System Settings; *Company & settings* shows it. - **Administration → Document masters → Document types** has a **Country** filter in its toolbar. It opens on the default country, showing that country's types and those of any country; pick another country, or *All countries*. - **A person's country** is their organisation's. - **Matching:** an organisation, and its people, can only have documents of their country's types or of types with no country. *Add document* offers only those, and the **Missing** section only counts those: an Indian client is never shown a UAE Trade License as missing. - **Changing a country:** an organisation cannot change country while it or its people hold documents of a type tied to its current country, and a document type cannot change country while it has documents of holders elsewhere.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Document Registration
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Document Registration

## The Document register (`/tracker/documents`)

**Register** in the sidebar opens the **Document register**: your actual organisations, people and their documents, the day-to-day records. (What kinds of holders, groups and documents exist is set up in Administration → Document masters, chapter 2.) It starts with three ways to browse the documents: **By organisation**, **By person** and **By group**. Client users see only their own organisations.

| Folder | Shows |
|---|---|
| By organisation → a holder type (*Our company*, *Client* …) | its organisations, with red and amber badges counting expired and expiring documents |
| an organisation | its **profile**: details, groups, its **people** as folders, and its documents by urgency (expired, expiring soon, under renewal, valid, not tracked), most urgent first. A **Missing** section lists required document types that are not on file. |
| a person (inside their organisation) | the person's profile and documents, in the same way |
| By person → a holder type (*Staff*, *Client contact*) | everyone of that type across organisations, searchable; each opens their profile |
| By group → a dimension (*Document category*, *Client category* …) | its groups, with badges, and **No group** when some documents have none in that dimension |
| By group → a dimension → a group | the documents in that group, by urgency, titled "type · holder"; the panel shows the group's managers and assignee in the selected company |

A document is in one group per dimension, so it appears once in each dimension: Al Noor Contracting's Trade License is under *Document category → Licences & permits* and under *Client category → Key account*. Both open the same document.

A file is one document:
- its type, number and expiry date with the days left;
- an urgency colour: **expired**, **expiring soon** (within the threshold), **under renewal**, **valid** or **not tracked** (disabled, or its holder is disabled);
- the assignee's initials.

### Add a document with AI

**Add a document with AI** (since 5.16.0). Document staff (Tracker Administrators, Company Administrators, Document Managers and Document Assignees who may add documents) can register a document from its file alone:
1. Attach the file (PDF, JPG, PNG or WEBP): drop it, paste it, browse, or take a photo on a phone.
2. DIGITZ AI reads it and fills a card: document type, holder, number, authority, issue and expiry dates. Each field says **Read from file**, **Please check** or **Not found**. A holder who is not in the tracker yet can be added from the card (a new person, with their organisation, or a new organisation). A document with the same type and number already registered is pointed out.
3. Check the card and press **Register and track**. Nothing is saved before that.
4. The document is tracked like any other: its assignee (see *Help → How an assignee is chosen*), reminders, and the AI check of its file.

The AI only reads the file and the names of your document types. It never sees your holders: matching the name on the file to a holder is done inside DIGITZ Tracker, in the selected company only. When the AI is switched off or has no key, the same window lets you fill the card yourself.

## Who sees what

| Role | Documents and cycles |
|---|---|
| Tracker Administrator | all |
| Document Manager | documents in a group they manage, and cycles they manage |
| Document Assignee | documents and cycles assigned to them |
| Client user | their own organisations' documents and their people's, read-only |
| others | none |

Staff with a tracker role see every organisation and person, as a directory, but only the documents the rules above give them.

**Administration → Masters** shows the same documents by **document type** and by **group**, most urgent first.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Expiry Automation & Alerts
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Expiry Automation & Alerts

The tracker sends ten kinds of e-mail, called **events**. Four go to the holder side, five to your own people, and one is a weekly summary for managers. Each Tracker Company switches every event on or off and chooses its template in **Administration → Company & settings → Notifications**.

## The events

| Event | Who gets it | When |
|---|---|---|
| **Expiry reminder (holder)** | the holder side | on each reminder day before the expiry date, and on the expiry day ("expires today") |
| **Expired (holder)** | the holder side | once, the day after the expiry date |
| **Waiting on you (holder)** | the holder side | when someone sets *Waiting on… → Holder*: what is needed (the note) and by when |
| **Renewed (holder)** | the holder side | when the document is renewed, with its new expiry date |
| **Expiry reminder** | your people | on each reminder day before the expiry date, and on the expiry day |
| **Expired** | your people | once, the day after the expiry date |
| **Assigned to you** | the new assignee | when a document gets a new assignee: a new validity cycle, *Reassign*, or a change in groups or types. Never when you assigned it to yourself. |
| **Waiting time over** | the assignee | once, when the *Waiting on…* date has come and the document is still waiting |
| **Reassign needed** | the document's managers | once, when the person it was reassigned to is no longer an employee |
| **Weekly summary** | each Document Manager | Mondays 08:00: expired, expiring, waiting and unassigned documents of their groups, with the 10 most urgent |

- **The holder side:** when the holder type has *Send reminders to the holder's organisation*, the reminder recipients of the holder's organisation; with *Also e-mail the person*, also the person's own e-mail.
- **Your people:** the reminder recipients of your company (its home organisation), the document's managers and its assignee.

Each address gets one copy, and disabled users get none.

## Reminder days

The reminder days are the company's **Reminder days before expiry** (for example `30, 15, 7, 1`) plus the expiry day. Every hour, and as soon as a cycle is created, the reminder due is the smallest reminder day at or above the days left; it is sent once and recorded on the cycle. A document added with 3 days left gets its 7-day reminder at once, and a missed hour or day is caught up. Closed cycles and documents that are not tracked get nothing.

## The e-mails

Every e-mail has the same layout:
- your company's logo (from Company & settings) or name;
- a coloured line saying what it is about: *Expiring soon*, *Expired*, *Action needed*, *Renewed*, *Assigned to you*, …;
- the message from the event's template;
- a table with the document, its number, the holder, the authority, the expiry date and, for your people, the assignee;
- for your people, an **Open document** button (the summary has **Open Team board**);
- a last line saying why the recipient gets it.

Holder e-mails are polite and plain and ask the holder to reply; internal ones are short and say what to do next. Every one ends with *Kind regards* and the sender's name, **Digitz Tracker - Support Team**.

## Templates

The templates are Email Templates named **Tracker · …** (for example *Tracker · Expired (holder)*); edit them in Desk → Email Template. Editing changes the subject and the message only; the layout stays. In Company & settings each event shows *Default (Tracker · …)* until you choose another template; switch an event **off** to send nothing.

What a template can use:

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `company` | your company's name |
| `holder`, `organisation`, `person` | the holder; its organisation; the person (blank for an organisation) |
| `document`, `document_no`, `authority` | the document type, its number and authority |
| `expiry_date`, `days_left`, `days_text` | the expiry date (22 Nov 2026), the days left, and in words ("in 12 days", "today", "3 days overdue") |
| `assignee_name`, `managers`, `recipient_title` | the assignee, the managers, the recipient's name |
| `record_url` | the link to the holder's page in `/tracker/documents` |
| `signature` | the sign-off: the name of the e-mail account the mail is sent from (*Digitz Tracker - Support Team*), so it matches the sender; through Amazon SES, the company name |
| `waiting_on_text`, `until`, `note` | *Waiting on you* and *Waiting time over*: on whom, until when, the note |
| `new_expiry_date`, `renewed_on` | *Renewed* |
| `assigned_by`, `reason` | *Assigned to you* |
| `manager_name`, `counts`, `rows` | *Weekly summary*: the manager, the four counts, the most urgent documents |

Templates written before version 4.7.0 keep working: `doc.company`, `doc.person`, `doc.document`, `doc.document_no`, `doc.authority`, `doc.expiry_date` and `doc.days_to_expire` are still there.

## WhatsApp

Each event can also go out on **WhatsApp**, alongside the e-mail or instead of it. This uses the frappe_whatsapp app and your Meta WhatsApp Business account (chapter 2).

- **Switch it on per event**, in Company & settings: tick **WhatsApp** on the event's row. It is off for every event until you tick it, because Meta charges per conversation. The e-mail switch is separate, so an event can go by e-mail, by WhatsApp or both.
- **Templates.** Each event has its own short WhatsApp template, `dzt_<event>` (for example `dzt_holder_expiry_reminder`: *Reminder from Al Noor Services: the Trade License (CN-1180022) of Al Noor Contracting expires on 22 Nov 2026, in 30 days. …*). Meta must approve a template before it can be sent. Until then, that event's WhatsApp is skipped (and noted in the Error Log), and its e-mail still goes.
- **Who receives it:** the same people as the e-mail, on their WhatsApp numbers:
  - an organisation's reminder recipients (their *WhatsApp number*; a recipient may have only a number);
  - users' *Mobile No* (assignee, managers, weekly summary);
  - a person's *Mobile*, when their holder type sends to the person.

  Numbers need the country code (`+971 50 123 4567`). A missing or invalid number skips that person on WhatsApp only.
- **Once only, per channel:** each reminder, expiry or renewal goes once on WhatsApp and once by e-mail; a failure on one never stops the other. The weekly summary sends its four counts.
- Every WhatsApp sent is in the Tracker Notification Log with channel *WhatsApp*, the number and the text, linked to its WhatsApp Message.

## Push to the mobile app

Staff who use the mobile app (chapter 12) also get the events meant for them as notifications on their phone:
- Expiry reminder
- Expired
- Assigned to you
- Waiting time over
- Reassign needed

Tapping one opens the document.

- **Switch it per event** in Company & settings: the **Push** column, on for every event by default (push costs nothing). Holder events and the weekly summary are not pushed.
- **Who receives it:** the same staff as the e-mail, on each phone where they are signed in and allowed notifications. Contacts without a user account get no push.
- **Once only, per channel**, like e-mail and WhatsApp. A push that fails never stops the e-mail.
- Push works only when the server's Firebase settings are in place (chapter 12 → *Setting up notifications*).

## If sending fails

The holder side and your people are sent separately: if one fails, the other still goes. A failure (for example, no outgoing e-mail account) is written to the Error Log and tried again at the next hourly run, without sending again what already went. A failed e-mail never stops the action that caused it (renewing, reassigning, waiting).

## Log and delivery

Every e-mail is recorded in **Tracker Notification Log** with its event, date, organisation, cycle, recipient, template and body. E-mails go through Frappe's e-mail queue, so the scheduler must run and one way of sending must be available (system readiness on Home checks it).

## How e-mails are sent

Set this in Desk → **DIGITZ Email Settings** → *Send system emails through*:

- **Amazon SES** (the default): on a DIGITZ PRIME workspace, e-mails are sent for you with nothing to set up. The sender shows your company name, *via DIGITZ PRIME*, and every template is signed with your company name. Replies go to the *Reply-To address* in the same settings, or to the workspace administrator when it is blank.
- **Outgoing Email Account**: e-mails, password resets and invitations use your default outgoing account in Desk → Email Account, and are signed with its name.

A site that is not a DIGITZ PRIME workspace uses its Email Account, unless DIGITZ PRIME has approved it for Amazon SES. *Currently sending through* on the same page shows the way in use. If the sending service is briefly unavailable, e-mails wait in the queue and are tried again, for up to 24 hours.

### Who can receive e-mail through Amazon SES

Amazon SES sends only to verified addresses:

- **Your users** receive e-mail straight away, as long as their user is enabled.
- **Anyone else**, such as a client contact, first gets a short message: *Confirm you want emails from* your company. Your e-mail goes within 5 minutes of them saying yes, and later e-mails go straight through.
- **If they do not confirm within 24 hours**, the e-mail ends in Error in the queue. It is not sent later, even if they confirm afterwards, so send it again. Ask new contacts to look out for the message.
- **An address that does not exist, or that reports spam,** is blocked, and e-mail to it ends in Error. Others on the same e-mail still receive theirs. If they say no to the confirmation message, the same applies.

If too many of your e-mails bounce or are reported as spam, your e-mail is put on hold and you are told. These rules do not apply when you send through your own Email Account.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Employee Assignments
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Employee Assignments

## Dimensions and groups

A document can be grouped in several ways at once, one group per **dimension**:

| Dimension (example) | Source | Groups (example) |
|---|---|---|
| Client category | the holder (clients) | Key account, Standard |
| Department | the holder (staff) | HR, PRO, Accounts |
| Document category | the document type | Licences & permits, Identity & licences |

For each enabled dimension, a document's group is the first that applies:
1. a group **set on the document itself** (a solid tag in its Groups field);
2. the dimension's source: the **document type's** group, or the **holder's** group;
3. for a person without a group in a holder-sourced dimension, **their organisation's** group.

A disabled group is skipped. A document may have no group in a dimension.

The Document register's **By group** folder lists, for each dimension, its groups and the documents in each (chapter 3).

**Help → How groups work** (since 5.17.0) explains this in the app. Open it with the **Help** button in the top bar, or with **How it works** on the readiness card **Groups** on Home, which is to do until every enabled dimension has at least one enabled group. Tracker Administrators, Company Administrators and Document Managers also see **In <company> now**: each enabled dimension (in assignment priority order, with its source and holder types), its groups and how many active documents of the selected company are in each, with any dimension that has no group yet marked.

### Which holders a dimension applies to

A dimension whose source is the holder can be limited to some **holder types** (Administration → Document masters → Group dimensions → **Applies to holder types**). For example, *Client category* applies to *Client* and *Department* to *Staff*, as installed. Leave it empty and the dimension applies to every holder.

- Only holders of those types show the dimension in their **Groups** field and can be given a group in it. In **Add person**, the dimensions follow the chosen holder type.
- The staff of an organisation still fall back to their organisation's group (step 3 above) when the organisation's type is in the scope.
- A dimension cannot be narrowed while holders outside the new scope have a group in it: remove those groups first.
- Groups are created in Document masters. The search box in **+ Add group** only filters the existing groups; when there are none, it says so.

## The assignee: one person does the work

Groups and document types are shared by all Tracker Companies, but **their people are per company**: a group has managers and an assignee in each company. A document only looks at those of its own company.

A document's assignee is the first valid user from:
1. the assignee set on the **document**;
2. the assignee of its **document type** in the document's company;
3. the assignees of its **groups** in the document's company, dimension by dimension in **assignment priority** order. For example, with Department before Document category, the HR assignee wins over the Licences assignee.

If none is found, the document is **Unassigned**. It then shows in the home tile and on the Expiry page, so it is never silently dropped.

A user is valid only when enabled, holding Document Assignee, Document Manager or Tracker Administrator, and an **employee of the document's company**. Anyone else is skipped. When the company has **Never assign a person's own document to them** ticked, the holder of a document is skipped too.

The document's panel says how the assignee was filled (**Assignee filled**): directly on the document, from the document type, from a group (with its dimension), set by hand on the cycle, or not filled.

**Help → How an assignee is chosen** (since 5.15.0) explains this rule in the app. Open it with the **Help** button in the top bar, or with the **How is it chosen?** links next to *Assignee filled*, the *Assignee* of a group or document type, the *Assignee in …* fields of their forms, and the readiness cards *Assignees* and *Assigned* on Home (*How it works*). Tracker Administrators, Company Administrators and Document Managers also see **In <company> now**: the document types and groups that have an assignee in the selected company (in the order the rule reads them, with anyone who would be skipped marked), the groups without one, how many open documents are unassigned, and who may be an assignee.

## Managers: everyone who oversees

A document's managers are the managers, in its company, of **all** its groups: the HR manager and the Identity & residency manager, for example. Each of them sees the document, receives its reminders and may reassign it. "Which kind of manager" is simply the dimension: a department manager, a category owner or an account manager.

## Keeping it current

Groups, assignee and managers are worked out again whenever something they depend on changes:
- the document itself, or its type;
- a group (its managers, assignee or disabled state);
- a dimension's source or priority;
- the holder's groups, or its organisation's;
- a user being disabled, or gaining or losing roles;
- an **employee leaving**: their person disabled, its user removed, or moved out of the company's own organisation.

When an employee leaves, their documents and open cycles go to the next valid assignee, or become Unassigned, and they stop being a manager. A cycle that was assigned to them by hand keeps them but is marked **Assignee left** and shows under **Unassigned** on the Team board, to be reassigned.

Open cycles follow these changes, with one exception: a cycle whose assignee was set by hand (**Reassign**) keeps that assignee. Closed cycles keep the people who handled them.

Large changes, affecting more than 200 documents, run in the background.

## Who sees what, by group

| Role | Sees |
|---|---|
| Document Manager | documents in groups they manage |
| Document Assignee | documents assigned to them (also through a hand-assigned open cycle) |

So access to documents is configured with groups. A new department with its own manager is a new group in the *Department* dimension, and the holders in that department are tagged with it.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Status Tracking
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Status Tracking

## The document panel

Clicking a file opens its panel, which shows:
- its facts;
- each group the document is in, and **where it came from** (from the document type, the holder, the organisation or the document itself);
- the **assignee** and its managers;
- **Assignee filled**: how the assignee was filled, wherever the document is opened (also from Administration → Masters): *Directly on this document*; *From the document type Trade License*; *From the group HR (Department)*; *Set by hand on this cycle (Reassign)*, with what the document itself would give; or *Not filled*;
- **every cycle**, newest first.

Its actions follow your rights:

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| Start renewal, Renew, Waiting on…, Resume, Note, Payment follow-up, Payment status | whoever may change the cycle: its assignee, its managers, Company and Tracker Administrators |
| Reassign (this cycle only; kept even if the configuration changes) | Document Managers, Company and Tracker Administrators (of the document's company) |
| Discontinue, Edit document | whoever may change the document |
| Deactivate / Reactivate (stops tracking; the cycles and history are kept) | whoever may change the document |
| Delete document (with its cycles and history; recorded in the Tracker Audit Log) | Company Administrators, Tracker Administrators |

A **missing** file explains why it is listed and offers **Add**.

## My work (`/tracker/work`)

An assignee's documents, in three sections, most urgent first:

| Section | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Needs action** | expired, expiring soon or under renewal, and not waiting |
| **Waiting** | parked with **Waiting on…** until a date. The card says who it waits on, e.g. "waiting on Sara Khan until 16 Oct". |
| **Coming up** | the rest that expire within the reminder horizon (the larger of the threshold and the largest reminder day) |

A card opens the same document panel as the explorer. Besides the renewal actions, it offers:
- **Waiting on…**, with one of four reasons:
  - **Holder**: the organisation or person the document belongs to (a client, a client's person or one of our own staff);
  - **Authority**: the document's issuing authority;
  - **Payment**;
  - **Other**: the note says what.

  It also takes a date (after today) and a note. On that date the document returns to *Needs action* by itself. Renewing or discontinuing clears it.
- **Resume**, which ends the waiting early.
- **Note**, a free-text entry.

**Activity:** every action on a cycle is listed in the panel's **Activity** section, newest first, with who and when. This covers opened, renewal started, waiting, resumed, notes, payment, reassigned, renewed, discontinued, and assignee changes made by the system. Client users do not see it.

**Team board:** Document Managers and Tracker Administrators also get a **Team** folder on this page. It has one folder per assignee, with their overdue and expiring counts and how many need action or are waiting, and an **Unassigned** folder. Opening a card there and choosing **Reassign** assigns it.
