DIGITZ Tracker — Files and AI Assistant
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Files and AI Assistant

## Files (`/tracker/files`)

**Documents → Files** shows the uploaded files like a file explorer on a computer: folders you open one inside the other, with the folder tree on the left, breadcrumbs, a search box and a grid or list view.

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| Organisations → a holder type → an organisation | its **people** (folders) and one **folder per document** ("Trade License", "CN-1180022 · 3 files") |
| an organisation → a person | that person's document folders |
| People → a holder type | everyone of that type who has files; each opens under their organisation |
| a document folder | its **files**: the current one first (*Current*), then those of earlier validity cycles (*Previous*) |

Only folders that contain files are shown. Each file has an icon with its type (PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX …), the cycle it belongs to, the upload date and its size. Opening it shows the details (document, holder, cycle, who uploaded it and when), a **preview** for pictures and PDFs, and **Open file**.

**AI check statistics.** The top of every Files page counts the current files of what you see by AI check: **Verified**, **Needs review**, **Failed**, **Pending** and **Not checked**. Click a count to show only those. Folders show a yellow badge for files to review and a red one for failed checks. A document folder ends with its result, for example *CN-1180022 · 2 files · Verified*. Inside it, the current file carries *AI: Verified* (or its other result). A file replaced after its check counts as *Not checked* until it is checked again.

You see the files of the documents you may see; a client's portal users see the files of their own organisations.

## AI assistant

Where your workspace has AI enabled, **AI Assistant** in the top bar answers questions about the documents you can see, such as "What expires in the next 30 days?". Answers use the same rules as the register: you only ever get documents your role and company allow. Each record links to its folder, and the text marked **AI interpretation** comes from the AI, not from your records. The assistant is read-only: it cannot renew, change, send or delete anything.

The built-in **Administrator** can use the AI Assistant when workspace AI is configured. Questions and document reads are scoped to the selected company. If the Assistant cannot load, a visible availability message appears.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Add-ons
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Add-ons

Some parts of DIGITZ Tracker are **add-ons**: optional modules that a company uses only when it needs them. The first one is **Services** (recurring client services and their tasks, Add-on: Services). Without an add-on, DIGITZ Tracker works fully for documents; the add-on's pages, menu items and Home tiles simply do not appear.

## How an add-on is turned on

1. **Register it for the installation.** In **Administration → Company & settings → Add-ons**, paste the add-on's **activation code** and click **Register**. The code comes from Techxcel Technologies. It names the add-on, your organisation and this site, and may have an end date.
2. **Switch it on for each company.** After registering, tick **On for <company>** on the add-on. Every company of the installation decides for itself; a code may limit how many companies can use it.

Only a **Tracker Administrator** can register, unregister and switch add-ons.

## What the page shows

For each add-on: its name and description, its **status**, who it is **licensed to**, **valid until** (or *no expiry*) and the beginning of the code's ID. The code itself is never shown again after registering.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Not registered | Not in use. Paste a code to register it. |
| Active | Registered. Switch it on for the companies that use it. |
| Expired: in grace period | The code's end date has passed. It keeps working for 14 days; register a new code. |
| Expired, Revoked | It no longer works. Its pages and menu items are hidden, and its records are kept. Register a new code. |
| Unregistered | A Tracker Administrator unregistered it. Its records are kept; registering again brings them back. |

When a code is refused, the page says why: it is for another add-on, another site, it has expired, it was revoked, or it is not a genuine code.

## When an add-on is off

- Its pages are not in the menu and open with a *not switched on* message.
- Its Home tiles are hidden, its masters are not offered under Service masters, and its background jobs do not run for that company.
- **Nothing is deleted.** When it is switched on again, everything is as it was.
- While an add-on is not registered at all, its records cannot be opened anywhere, Desk included (Administrator excepted).

Home's **System readiness** lists an add-on only when it is switched on for the company but its registration has lapsed.

## Upgrading from earlier versions

An installation that already used Services before 5.0.0 keeps it: the upgrade registers Services as *Existing installation* (no code needed) and switches it on for the companies that had not disabled services tracking.

## For developers and the vendor

Each add-on has a **Tracker Add-on** record (its registration for the installation, read-only) and each company a **Tracker Company Add-on** row per add-on it switched on.


The add-on mechanism and how other apps declare their own add-ons are described in `digitz_tracker/addons/TECHNICAL.md`. Activation codes are issued with `tools/addon_codes/` (`TECHNICAL.md` there). The private signing key never leaves the vendor.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Client Portal
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Client Portal The client portal is your clients' own view of DIGITZ Tracker, written from their side: what we need from them, what they can send us, where each renewal stands, and their requests and services. Staff review what clients send, answer their requests, and can preview any client's portal. ## Client users An organisation's **portal users** are users with only the **Client** role; the app refuses other roles. A portal user may belong to several organisations. They sign in at `/tracker/login` and never need Desk. Their Home opens **Your portal** (`/tracker/portal`); the staff pages (Register, Files, Services, Requests) are not open to them. ## Giving clients access From the organisation in the Document register: - **Invite portal user** (Tracker Administrators and Document Managers): enter the person's name and e-mail. A new address gets an account with only the Client role, and an e-mail to set their password. An address that already belongs to a client user is simply added; an address of a staff member, a disabled user or Administrator is refused. - **Edit organisation → Portal users**: add existing client users, or remove one with ×. Removing only takes away access to this organisation; the account stays. ## What clients see The portal has four tabs. With several organisations, a switcher at the top shows one organisation or all of them. | Tab | What it shows | |---|---| | **Overview** | A greeting and four counts (needs your attention, renewals in progress, valid documents, uploads under review), then **Needs your attention**, most urgent first, each with an **Upload** button:
  • *We're waiting on you*: a renewal we have parked as waiting on the holder, with our note and the date we need it by;
  • *Upload not accepted*: their last upload was rejected, with our reason;
  • *Expired*: a document that has expired and whose renewal has not started;
  • *Missing*: a document their holder type requires that is not on file;
  • *Expiring soon*: a document expiring within the company's threshold, renewal not started.
Beside it, their recent uploads and requests with their status. | | **Documents** | Every document of their organisations and people, grouped by holder, with a plain status (*Valid until …*, *Expires in 12 days*, *Renewal in progress*, *Waiting on you*, *Expired*) and a **timeline**: issued, each renewal, renewal in progress, waiting on you, expiry. Filters: all, needs attention, in renewal, valid. A document's file opens; **Send a new version** uploads one. Below, their uploads with *Under review*, *Accepted* or *Not accepted* and the reason. | | **Requests** | *Ask us something* (subject, request) and *How are we doing?* (1–5 stars, comments), then their requests (*Sent* or *Seen*) and feedback. These are **Client Request** and **Client Feedback** records, for the organisation they choose. | | **Services** | When the Services add-on is on: their services (billing frequency, next due date) and the periods with *In progress*, *Completed*, *Unpaid* or *Paid*. | Never shown to clients: who works on a document (assignee, managers), groups, our internal notes and activity, the AI check, and our employees on service tasks. ## Uploads and their review A client's upload becomes a **Client Submission**; it does not change the document until someone reviews it. 1. The client clicks **Upload** (or *Send a new version*), chooses the file and may add a note. The item shows *Under review*; one upload per document is reviewed at a time. 2. Staff see it under **Client portal → Submissions** (`/tracker/submissions`), and Home shows a **Client uploads to review** tile. Each submission shows the client, holder, document, the note and the file. 3. **Accept**: the file becomes the document's current file (the AI check runs on it as usual). If the renewal was waiting on the client, it resumes. For a missing document, enter its number and dates: the document is created with the file. 4. **Reject**: give a reason. The client sees it on their Overview and can upload again. Document Managers and Document Assignees review submissions of the documents they can change; accepting a missing document needs permission to add documents. ## Preview a client's portal **Client portal → Preview** (`/tracker/portal/preview`) shows the portal exactly as a client sees it, read-only, under a *Previewing as …* banner: - by **organisation**: any organisation you can open. Each one says how many portal users it has, or *no portal users yet*: its portal can be previewed, but nobody can sign in to it until you invite someone; - by **portal user**: all of that user's organisations in the selected company, as they see them after signing in. Nothing can be uploaded or sent from a preview. Staff never have a portal of their own: opening `/tracker/portal` takes them to Preview, and their sidebar has no *Your portal*. ## E-mails to clients Reminders and other e-mails to a holder's contacts carry an **Open your portal** button when the organisation has portal users. ## Requests Staff with the Tracker Administrator or Service Manager role see all requests and feedback under **Client portal → Requests** and mark them read; the client then sees *Seen*.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Expiry and Home Overview
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Expiry and Home Overview

| Need | Where |
|---|---|
| What needs attention today | `/tracker/home` (*Home* below): expired, expiring soon, under renewal and **unassigned** documents, documents whose required **file is missing**; open tasks and unpaid services. All are counted for the signed-in user. |
| My own work, and my team's | **My work** (`/tracker/work`): needs action, waiting and coming up; managers also get the Team board (chapter 3) |
| Every open cycle by date | **Expiry** (`/tracker/expiry`): open cycles soonest first, as a list or a month calendar. Each row shows its holder, urgency and assignee, and links to the holder's folder. Chips filter by Expired, Expiring, Under renewal and Unassigned. |
| Documents by holder | the Document register (chapter 3) |
| Documents by type or group | **Administration → Masters** → a document type or a group: every document in it, most urgent first |
| Services by client and period | the services explorer (chapter 5) |
| Raw data | Desk lists of Tracked Document, Document Cycle, Employee Service Task and Service Record (filters, group-by, export), for administrators |

All of them follow the record rules: a manager or assignee sees only the documents that are theirs.

## Home

When you open Home after signing in, the **Add a document with AI** window opens over the page (once per sign-in; *Not now* closes it). The **+ Add with AI** button at the bottom right opens it at any time. See chapter 3 → *Add a document with AI*. It is offered to document staff who may add documents.

Home shows, for the selected company:

1. **System readiness** (Tracker Administrators only), first on the page because it is required set-up: a percentage of checks done, how many are still to do, and a card for each check.
   - Checks still to do come first in each part, marked **To do**, with what is missing and a **Fix** link to the page where it is set (or the name of the Desk screen).
   - Every card shows what is behind it, for example *Employees: 4 staff · 3 with users · 1 without*, *Users & roles: 1 Global Administrator · 1 Company Administrator · 2 Document Managers · 5 Document Assignees · 3 client portal users* (with the list of people and their roles), *Clients: 12 clients*. Where there is a list, **Show** opens up to 10 names (each opening its page), with **View all** when there are more.
   - *Setup*: default country, home organisation, document types for its country, employees, a document manager, assignees, reminders, notifications (every event that is on has a template), outgoing e-mail, WhatsApp (nothing on WhatsApp, or the app, a default account and approved templates for the events that use it), AI file check (an OpenAI key is set, or the check is switched off).
   - *Data*: our own required documents on file, clients added, every open document assigned.
   - When every check is done, the panel shrinks to one line, **System ready**, which still opens the cards.
2. **The counts**, each opening its page.
3. **The dashboard**, from the documents you may see:
   - **Documents by status**: one bar split into expired, under renewal, expiring, valid and not tracked, with the counts in its legend;
   - **Expiries in the next 6 months**: how many active documents expire each month;
   - **Needs attention by category**: expired and expiring documents per group;
   - **Workload** (Document Managers and Tracker Administrators): open documents per assignee, unassigned last;
   - **Next expiries**: the 8 soonest, each opening its holder.

   Hover over, or tab to, a bar to see its value.

The 21 Desk script reports, 4 workspaces, 12 number cards and 5 dashboard charts that came with the port of benchmark_operations were removed on 2026-10-13 in favour of these views.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Classic Navigation and Desk Access
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Classic Navigation and Desk Access

## Desk access (digitz_ui)

DIGITZ Tracker requires the **digitz_ui** app, which restricts Frappe Desk:

| User | Desk |
|---|---|
| Administrator | always |
| others | only with **Allow DIGITZ Desk Access** ticked on the user (System Managers set it) |

**Signing in on a DIGITZ page never gives Desk.** A session started at `/tracker/login` (or digitz_erp's `/classic/login`) cannot open Desk, whoever the user is, Administrator included: Desk links are hidden and Desk addresses answer *403*. To use Desk, sign out and sign in on Frappe's own page, `/login`.

Users without it are sent to their classic home page; Desk URLs answer *403 · Access restricted*. The restriction is on from installation. Turn it off per site with `bench --site <site> set-config -p digitz_desk_restriction 0`. List users to review with `bench --site <site> execute digitz_ui.desk_access.setup.list_desk_candidates`.

## The front end

The tracker's user interface is a set of pages outside Desk, on digitz_ui's theme (DIGITZ Classic: petrol teal, amber, green) and shell. The sidebar shows *DIGITZ* with *Tracker* and only the pages the user's roles allow.

| Route | Page | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | the site's address opens the tracker: home when signed in, otherwise sign-in | live |
| `/tracker` | redirects to home or sign-in | live |
| `/tracker/login` | sign-in | live |
| `/tracker/company` | choose the Tracker Company to work in; on a site with no company yet, a Tracker Administrator creates it here | live |
| `/tracker/home` | the user's own counts: expired, expiring, under renewal and unassigned documents, open tasks, unpaid services | live |
| `/tracker/documents` | the Document register (sidebar: Register): documents by organisation, by person and by group, as folders and files | live |
| `/tracker/files` | Files: the uploaded document files in their holder and document folders | live |
| `/tracker/work` | My work: needs action, waiting, coming up; the Team board for managers | live |
| `/tracker/expiry` | open cycles: list and calendar | live |
| `/tracker/services` | services as folders and files, task checklists | live |
| `/tracker/requests` | client requests and feedback (staff) | live |
| `/tracker/portal` | the client portal (client users; chapter 6) | live |
| `/tracker/portal/preview` | preview a client's portal (staff) | live |
| `/tracker/submissions` | client uploads to review (staff) | live |
| `/tracker/admin/…` | administration: holder types, group dimensions and groups, document types, other masters, **Users & roles** (the selected company's staff), **Company & settings** (the selected company; every company for Tracker Administrators) | live |

The sidebar shows only the pages your roles **in the selected company** allow, and never Desk links.

The sidebar groups the pages by the kind of work:

| Heading | Pages | For |
|---|---|---|
| (none) | Home; **Your portal** for client users | everyone |
| **Renewals** | My work, Expiry | acting on expiring documents: the daily work, so it comes first |
| **Documents** | Register, Files | looking up organisations, people, documents and their files |
| **Services** | Services | the Services add-on, when it is on |
| **Client portal** | Submissions, Requests, Preview | what clients send us, and their view (chapter 6) |
| **Administration** | Masters, Service masters, Users & roles, Company & settings | the catalogue, the company's staff and their roles, the settings |

Client users see only Home and **Your portal** (chapter 6); their Home opens the portal.

## The DIGITZ Tracker logo

The DIGITZ Tracker wordmark comes with the app, so every installation has it. It is shown in the sidebar of every page, on the sign-in page (`/tracker/login`) and at the top of the e-mails (unless the company has uploaded its own logo in Company & settings). It is also put in Frappe's own logo settings (Navbar and Website Settings: the app logo and the loading screen), but only where they are empty or point to a missing file, so a logo you set yourself, or DIGITZ ERP's on a shared site, is kept.

Every `bench migrate` checks this again and restores the logo where it has gone missing.

## Choosing and switching the company

Everything in the tracker belongs to the **selected Tracker Company**.
- After signing in, a user who may use **one** company goes straight in. A user with **several** first sees the chooser at `/tracker/company`, with the last one used at the top, and then the page they asked for.
- The sidebar shows the selected company; clicking it, or **Switch company** in the settings menu, opens the chooser. After switching you land on Home.
- The choice belongs to the sign-in session, so other open tabs follow it. If your access to a company is removed, or it is disabled, you are asked to choose again.
- The tracker's company is chosen separately from digitz_erp's.

After signing in, a user without Desk access lands on `/tracker/home` if the tracker is the first DIGITZ app they may use (any tracker role). Themes are chosen in **DIGITZ Theme Settings** (digitz_ui).

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Mobile App
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Mobile App

The DIGITZ Tracker app puts the day-to-day work on the phone: what is expiring, what is assigned to you, recording a renewal with a photo of the new document, and adding documents. Everything you do in the app is what you can do in the tracker in a browser, except administration, which stays on the desktop.

The app shows your company's own site, so it always has the latest version of the screens. It adds what a phone does best: the camera, and notifications.

## Getting started

1. Install **DIGITZ Tracker** on your phone.
2. Enter your **workspace**: the first part of your site's address. For `acme.digitztracker.com`, enter `acme`. The app checks that it is a DIGITZ Tracker site and remembers it.
3. **Sign in** with the same e-mail and password as on the desktop. You stay signed in when you close the app, until you sign out or your session expires.
4. If you work for several companies, choose one. The company is shown at the top of every screen; tap it to switch.

To use another workspace, open **More → Change workspace**. This signs you out.

You can also open the same screens in a phone's browser at `https://<your site>/mobile`. They work the same, but without notifications.

## Look

The app looks like DIGITZ on the desktop: it takes the colours, typeface and style of the active DIGITZ theme (chosen in **DIGITZ Theme Settings**, chapter 8), so a theme change shows in the app too. On a phone, the menu is a row of tabs at the bottom instead of the sidebar. The app's icon is the DIGITZ **D**, the same as the site's browser icon.

## Screens

The tabs at the bottom are **Home · My work · Expiry · Register · More**. You see only the ones your roles allow in the selected company.

| Screen | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Home** | Your counts: expired, expiring soon, under renewal, unassigned, uploads missing, client uploads to review. Tap a count to open its list. |
| **Home** (top) | **Scan or attach a document** (see below). |
| **My work** | Your documents in three sections: **Needs action**, **Waiting**, **Coming up**, most urgent first. Document Managers switch to **Team** to see each assignee's documents and the unassigned ones. |
| **Expiry** | Every open renewal you may see, month by month. Filter: expired, expiring, under renewal, unassigned. |
| **Register** | **Search** organisations, people and documents by name or number, or browse by organisation, person or group. An organisation or person shows their details and their documents, with **Add document**. |
| **Document** | Its status, details, file, cycles and activity, and the actions you may take. |
| **More** | Switch company, Diagnostics (a check of the app, the camera and notifications), Change workspace, Sign out. |

## Working on a document

The main actions are buttons at the top of a document; the rest are under **⋯**. They are the same as on the desktop, with the same permissions:
- Start renewal, **Renew** (new expiry date, renewal date, and a photo of the renewed document), Waiting on…, Resume, Note
- Payment follow-up, Payment status, Reassign (Document Managers)
- Edit document, Check again (the AI check of the file), Deactivate / Reactivate, Discontinue, Delete (administrators)

Discontinue, Deactivate and Delete ask you to confirm first.

**Files of documents.** Wherever a form asks for a file, there are two buttons:
- **Scan**: the phone's document scanner. It finds the page edges, crops and straightens, cleans up the image, and takes several pages, which become one PDF.
- **Attach a file**: a PDF or photo already on the phone (Files, Downloads, Photos, Drive, a WhatsApp attachment).

**Adding a document.** Open the holder in the Register and tap **Add document**. A missing document listed on a holder can be added from the missing item itself.

## Scan or attach a document

The quickest way to file a paper document: **Scan or attach a document** on Home, or the camera button on My work and Register.
1. Choose **Scan with the camera** or **Attach a file from this phone**.
2. Say what it is:
   - **A new document**: find the organisation or person, then fill in the form. The file is already attached.
   - **A new file for a document**: find the document (by number, type or holder), then choose:
     - **Renew with this file**: a new validity period, with this file as the renewed document
     - **Replace the current file**: the same period, a better copy

     You see only what your role allows for that document.
3. Save. The app opens the document and shows **Checking the file…** while the AI check reads it, as on the desktop (chapter 3). The result (*Verified*, *Needs review*, *Not checked* or *Failed*) appears on its own.

On Android the scanner comes from Google Play services, which installs it the first time it is used. On a phone without it, the camera takes a plain photo.

The AI check runs in the background: on a server, `bench start` (or the production workers) must be running, as for the desktop.

## Notifications

When notifications are on, staff receive on their phone the events that are meant for them:
- Expiry reminder
- Expired
- Assigned to you
- Waiting time over
- Reassign needed

Tapping a notification opens the document, in the right company.

The app asks for permission on Home (**Get notified → Turn on**). Each event can be switched off for push in **Company & settings → Notifications** (the **Push** column, on by default). Push needs the server's Firebase settings (see *Setting up notifications* below). Holders and clients do not receive pushes yet. They get e-mail and WhatsApp as before.

Each phone that allows notifications is registered as a **Tracker Mobile Device** of its user. Signing out removes it, so that phone stops receiving the user's notifications.

## Not in the app

Administration stays on the desktop:
- creating companies
- organisations, people and portal users
- document masters (types, categories, groups, authorities, designations)
- services and templates
- users and roles
- settings, add-ons, AI and WhatsApp
- the client portal preview

Not yet in the app: the client portal for client users, Submissions, Requests and Services. These come in the next releases.

A PDF file opens as a download on Android; images open in the app.

## Setting up notifications (administrators)

1. Create a Firebase project for the app, with the Android and iOS apps, and upload the APNs key for iOS.
2. Copy the Firebase service account file to the server, then run:
   ```
   bench set-config -g digitz_fcm_service_account /path/to/service-account.json
   bench set-config -g digitz_fcm_project_id <project id>
   ```
3. On a phone, open **More → Diagnostics → Send me a test notification**.

The key is a file on the server and stays there; it is never stored in the site or sent to phones.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — DIGITZ PRIME Workspaces
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — DIGITZ PRIME Workspaces

A company that signs up on digitztracker.com gets its own DIGITZ Tracker workspace at `<name>.digitztracker.com`, created automatically by DIGITZ PRIME. This chapter describes what is different in such a workspace. A site installed any other way (your own server, a test site) behaves exactly as described in the other chapters: none of this applies there.

## Activating the administrator account

After the workspace is ready you receive, by email and WhatsApp, the workspace link, your administrator email and a one-time activation code. No password is ever sent.

1. Open the link. The **Activate your workspace** page opens at `/activate`.
2. Enter your administrator email and the activation code.
3. Choose a password (at least 10 characters, mixing words, numbers or symbols) and confirm it.
4. Select **Activate and sign in**. You are signed in and the tracker's home page opens.

The code works once and expires (72 hours by default). **Send me a new code** sends a fresh one and the previous code stops working. You are a **Tracker Administrator**: you add your staff in *Users & roles* as usual.

## Subscription page and notices

`/subscription` shows the status of the workspace (trial, active, expired, suspended), the date it is valid until (UTC), the days left, and **Renew or upgrade**, which opens the DIGITZ PRIME billing portal. **Refresh status** asks DIGITZ PRIME for the latest status straight away, for example just after a payment.

A banner at the top of the tracker pages reminds you during a trial, in the last 7 days of a subscription, and when the workspace is working offline.

## When the subscription ends

At the exact end time, the workspace stops normal work: tracker pages open the subscription page instead, changes to records are refused, and reminders and other scheduled jobs pause. You can still sign in, see the subscription page, renew and sign out. **Nothing is deleted**: renewing restores everything as it was, on the same address. A suspended workspace behaves the same way until DIGITZ support lifts the suspension.

## Sample data in a trial

When you sign up for a trial you can tick **Fill my trial with sample data**. Your workspace then fills itself once, right after it is built: 8 demo staff (people only, they use none of your trial's users), 15 UAE clients and their documents, with expiry dates relative to the day of your trial. You become the employee who looks after every document type (Document Manager), so every sample document has you as its assignee.

- **Sample records never send messages**: no e-mail, WhatsApp or push about them, and they are not in your digest.
- **They do not count towards your plan's document limit.**
- **Remove sample data**: on Home, administrators see a *Sample data* card while sample records exist. *Remove sample data* deletes them all; your own records are kept (a sample client to which you added a real document is kept too). Sample data is never added again.

## Plan limits

Your plan sets limits that the tracker applies when something is added:

| Limit | What counts |
|---|---|
| Companies | enabled Tracker Companies |
| Staff users | enabled users with a staff role (Tracker Administrator, Company Administrator, Document Manager, Document Assignee, Service Manager, Service Executive); client portal users do not count |
| Active documents | tracked documents that are neither disabled nor inactive |
| File storage | the total size of the files in the workspace |

When a limit is reached, adding one more is refused with a message; disabling or archiving frees a place. WhatsApp notifications and the Services add-on are available only when the plan includes them.

## Behind the scenes

- **Tracker Subscription** (a single, read-only record) holds the workspace's signed entitlement from DIGITZ PRIME: status, validity, plan features and limits, and when it was last confirmed. Nobody can edit it; the tracker re-checks the signature every time it decides, so changing the record would grant nothing.
- **Tracker Quota Lock** holds one row per limit, used so that two people adding at the same moment cannot pass a limit together.
- The workspace confirms its subscription every hour. If DIGITZ PRIME cannot be reached it keeps working for up to two more days (never past the end of the subscription), then pauses until it can confirm again.

These records belong to the module **Tracker Subscription** (`tracker_subscription`). Technical design: `digitz_tracker/tracker_subscription/TECHNICAL.md`.

## System email in managed workspaces

When DIGITZ PRIME enables central system email for your workspace, password-reset and account invitation emails come from the platform's no-reply sender. The link opens your own workspace. Failed deliveries are retried while the link remains valid. Ask for a fresh reset if it expires. Your workspace holds no SES credentials. Standalone installations and managed sites without this option keep their own configured outgoing mail. Business notifications keep their existing mail settings.

Administrators can inspect **Tracker System Email** delivery records to see whether an account email is pending, accepted centrally, failed or expired. Records retain delivery metadata; reset tokens are encrypted temporarily and removed after hand-off or final failure. Accepted means the management site has queued the email, not that it has reached the inbox.

entries.title: DIGITZ Tracker — Services Add-on
entries.content:
# DIGITZ Tracker — Services Add-on

**Services is an add-on** (chapter 5): it appears only after it is registered for the installation with an activation code and switched on for the company. Its records live in the module **Tracker Services**. Installations that already used services before version 5.0.0 keep it without a code.

## Service records

A **Service Record** sells a **Service** to a client organisation. It records:
- the client, the service and the billing frequency (from the service);
- the **Service Due Date**;
- the task and prerequisite templates (copied from the service);
- optionally, its own manager, executive and prerequisites executive.

There can be only one per client, service and frequency. Disabled records stop producing tasks.

The manager, executive and prerequisites executive are **users**: a service record's own values win, otherwise the service's apply. Disabled users are skipped.

## Tasks

Saving a service record creates the task for the current period. Every hour, every enabled record is checked again:

| Frequency | One task per | Next due date |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly | month | + 1 month, when it falls in the current month |
| Quarterly | quarter | + 3 months |
| Yearly | year | + 12 months |
| Two Years | two-year cycle counted from the Service Due Date | + 24 months |
| One Time | record (once) | the Service Due Date |

An **Employee Service Task** holds:
- the client, service, period and due date;
- the status: Unassigned, Assigned, On Going, Completed, Unpaid or Paid Or Settled;
- the manager, the executive and the prerequisites executive;
- two checklists copied from the templates, **tasks** and **prerequisites**; each prerequisite is due on the task's due date.

The task counts what is still open. The manager is always set. The executives are set only when **Assign service tasks automatically** is on, and the task then starts as Assigned.

## Who sees what

| Role | Tasks |
|---|---|
| Tracker Administrator | all |
| Service Manager | tasks where they are the manager |
| Service Executive | tasks assigned to them, or whose prerequisites are assigned to them |
| Client user | their own organisations' tasks, read-only |
| others | none |

Ticking a checklist item saves the task, so it needs permission to edit that task.

## Screens

**Services** (`/tracker/services`) shows them as **folders and files**: client organisation → service → one file per billing period, with its status and progress bars for tasks and prerequisites. A file opens the task, where you tick checklist items and set the status.
